12	
13	## Problem
14	
15	Shared-folder write operations are the one remaining folder-state-mutating web
16	path that does NOT route through the SDK client. `useSharedWriteOps`
17	(apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedWriteOps.ts) calls the sdk shared-write functions
18	**directly**, each with a `SharedWriteContext` built from local refs
19	(`folderChildrenRef` / `sequenceNumberRef` in `useSharedNavigation`), never
20	touching `client.folderTree`:
21	
22	- `uploadToSharedFolder` (line 138)
23	- `createSharedSubfolder` (line 189)
24	- `renameInSharedFolder` (line 236)
25	- `updateSharedFile` (line 275)
26	- `deleteFromSharedFolder` (line 346)
27	
28	Phase 47 (PR #494) made the SDK client the single owner of **owned** folder state:
29	file replace, version restore/delete, folder CRUD, and bin ops now all route
30	through `getSdkClient().<method>()`, with the client owning publish + sequence
31	bookkeeping + the `folder:updated` emission. A full audit confirmed every owned
32	mutation is routed; shared-folder writes are the lone exception because shared
33	folders aren't tracked in `client.folderTree` — they have a separate key/context
34	model (`SharedWriteContext`). This is the same desync class the owned-folder work
35	eliminated (store/refs drifting from the authoritative tree, stale-sequence 409s,
36	edit-beats-delete resurrection), scoped to shared folders.
37	
38	## Solution
39	
40	Teach the SDK client to own shared-folder state, then route `useSharedWriteOps`
41	through it (mirrors the owned-folder consolidation):
42	
43	- Decide whether shared folders join the existing `folderTree` or a sibling
44	  `sharedFolderTree` keyed by share — they carry a distinct key/context
45	  (`SharedWriteContext`), so a parallel structure is likely cleaner.
46	- Add client methods (e.g. `uploadToSharedFolder` / `createSharedSubfolder` /
47	  `renameInSharedFolder` / `updateSharedFile` / `deleteFromSharedFolder`) that own
48	  the publish + sequence bookkeeping + a `folder:updated`-style emission internally.
49	- Make `useSharedNavigation`'s `folderChildrenRef` / `sequenceNumberRef` a
50	  projection fed by those events — never written from the write hook directly.
51	
52	**Scope:** medium, multi-PR. Not a correctness blocker today (shared folders are a
53	self-contained state model, so there is no cross-contamination with the owner's
54	`folderTree`), but it leaves shared folders outside the single-ownership invariant
55	and re-exposes the desync footgun for any new shared-write path.
56	
57	**References:** PR https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/494 (owned-folder
58	consolidation + the audit that surfaced this gap). Related but distinct todos:
59	`2026-06-14-unify-folder-state-ownership-in-sdk-client.md` (owned-folder
60	counterpart, largely delivered by PR #494) and
61	`2026-06-14-updatesharedfile-discards-prunedcids-from-updatefilemetadata.md`
62	(shared-file pin-leak in the same sdk share-write module).

17	
18	## Problem
19	
20	PR #498 made `CipherBoxClient` self-bootstrap `folderTree` from the root IPNS key
21	(`ensureFolderLoaded`, reached via the `requireFolder` chokepoint). Two things are
22	now redundant but were intentionally left in place so the self-heal could prove
23	out without widening that PR's blast radius:
24	
25	1. **The ~16 web `ensureFolderRegistered` call sites** (`apps/web/src/lib/sdk-provider.ts:96`
26	   defines it; callers in `useFolderMutations.ts`, `useFileOperations.ts:80`,
27	   `useFileVersions.ts:66`, `useDropUpload.ts:109`) pre-seed `folderTree` before
28	   every mutation. They are now no-ops — the SDK self-heals if the folder is
29	   absent. `useBin.ts:73/128` never had them and is already fixed by the SDK.
30	
31	2. **The web `useFolderNavigation.ts:233-240` unwrap path** duplicates the SDK's
32	   ECIES unwrap of `folderKeyEncrypted` / `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted`. This is a
33	   two-sources-of-truth smell (the SDK-helper-drift class) — the two copies must
34	   stay in lockstep.
35	
36	Separately, the security review flagged a MEDIUM: `ensureFolderLoaded` re-walks
37	the whole reachable tree on a cache miss for an **unreachable / server-withheld**
38	target, with no negative cache — self-inflicted amplification only if an upstream
39	caller tight-loops on an unresolvable target.
40	
41	## Solution
42	
43	Once self-bootstrap has proven out in staging/prod:
44	
45	1. Delete the web `ensureFolderRegistered` helper and its call sites; rely on the
46	   SDK chokepoint. Verify each former call site still works cold (reload → mutate
47	   into a never-navigated subfolder).
48	2. Make `useFolderNavigation` call `client.ensureFolderLoaded(ipnsName)` and read
49	   back the loaded `FolderState` instead of unwrapping keys itself; delete the
50	   web-side unwrap+register code so the unwrap logic lives only in the SDK.
51	3. **Only if** web/FUSE retry loops on unresolvable targets appear: add a
52	   short-lived per-target negative memo (or a walked-folder cap) inside
53	   `ensureFolderLoaded` (`packages/sdk/src/client.ts`). Not needed today — real
54	   callers target reachable folders and short-circuit on first hit.
55	
56	### Related
57	
58	- `[[route-shared-folder-writes-through-the-sdk-client]]` — adjacent SDK-ownership
59	  cleanup (shared-write paths). Both move state authority into the SDK.
60	- Supersedes the symptom-patch class tracked in the completed self-bootstrap todo
61	  (`2026-06-16-sdk-client-self-bootstrap-folder-tree-from-root-ipns-key`).

1	---
2	created: 2026-02-22T00:00
3	title: Research CRDT-based IPNS inbox for serverless share discovery
4	area: architecture
5	related:
6	  - .planning/todos/pending/2026-02-21-ipns-resolution-alternatives.md
7	  - .planning/phases/14-user-to-user-sharing/14-CONTEXT.md
8	  - .planning/todos/pending/2026-02-21-move-root-folder-key-to-ipfs.md
9	---
10	
11	## Summary
12	
13	Research using CRDTs over IPNS as a decentralized share discovery mechanism, replacing the centralized `shares` table. This is part of a broader strategy to solve IPNS write-conflict issues once as a horizontal concern rather than working around them per-feature.
14	
15	## Context
16	
17	Phase 14 chose server-side share records (PostgreSQL `shares`/`share_keys` tables) over metadata-embedded ACLs. The server knows the sharing graph (who shared with whom) but never sees plaintext keys. This was the right pragmatic tradeoff, but it moves further from the serverless ideal.
18	
19	A recurring pattern across CipherBox: every time we hit an IPNS limitation (write conflicts, resolution flakiness, last-writer-wins), we bolt on a centralized workaround (DB-cached CIDs, share tables, pinned_cids tracking). Each workaround is individually reasonable, but collectively they erode the serverless premise. Solving IPNS reliability and conflict resolution as a horizontal concern would unblock multiple features simultaneously.
20	
21	## Core Idea: IPNS Inbox with CRDT Content Model
22	
23	### Share Discovery via Deterministic IPNS Address
24	
25	Derive a per-recipient IPNS "inbox" address from their public key:
26	
27	```text
28	inbox_ipns_privkey = HKDF(recipient_pubkey, info="share-inbox")
29	inbox_ipns_name    = derive_public(inbox_ipns_privkey)
30	```
31	
32	- Sharers publish encrypted share invitations (ECIES-wrapped keys) to the recipient's inbox
33	- Recipients resolve their own inbox IPNS to discover shares
34	- Content encrypted so only recipient can decrypt
35	- Server never sees the sharing graph
36	
37	### Why CRDTs Solve the Write-Conflict Problem
38	
39	The naive IPNS inbox has a fundamental issue: IPNS is last-writer-wins, so concurrent shares from different users overwrite each other. CRDTs (Conflict-free Replicated Data Types) turn this weakness into a feature:
40	
41	- **G-Set (Grow-only Set):** Share invitations are append-only — new shares are added, never removed from the inbox. A G-Set merges concurrent additions without conflict.
42	- **OR-Set (Observed-Remove Set):** If revocation needs to remove entries, OR-Set supports both add and remove with deterministic conflict resolution.
43	- Each write includes the full CRDT state. Concurrent writers produce valid states that merge on read.
44	
45	### Cross-Cutting Benefit
46	
47	The same CRDT-over-IPNS pattern applies to other conflict-prone areas:
48	
49	- **Folder metadata sync** — concurrent edits from multiple devices
50	- **Device registry** — multiple devices registering simultaneously
51	- **Share inbox** — multiple sharers publishing to the same recipient
52	- **Any future multi-writer state**
53	
54	Solving this once gives all features coordination-free merging.
55	
56	## Known Challenges to Investigate
57	
58	### Write Access Control
59	
60	If the IPNS private key is derivable from public information (recipient's pubkey), anyone can publish to the inbox. Possible mitigations:
61	
62	- **Spam tolerance via encryption:** Attacker can write junk but can't forge valid encrypted invitations (would need to know a valid share key)
63	- **Signed envelopes:** Each invitation signed by the sharer's key — recipient verifies sender authenticity and ignores unsigned/invalid entries
64	- **Per-pair ECDH channels:** `HKDF(ECDH(sharer_priv, recipient_pub), info="share-channel")` — only the two parties can derive the key. But kills open discovery (recipient must try ECDH with every known pubkey)
65	
66	### IPNS Reliability
67	
68	This approach makes IPNS reliability _more_ critical, not less. Pairs with the sibling IPNS resolution alternatives todo — any solution there directly benefits this approach.
69	
70	### Revocation
71	
72	Currently a DB flag (`revoked_at`). With IPNS inbox:
73	
74	- Sharer can't "un-publish" an invitation the recipient already cached
75	- Revocation becomes eventually-consistent at best
76	- May need to separate "discovery" (inbox) from "access" (key rotation) — revoke by rotating the shared folder's key, not by modifying the inbox
77	
78	### State Size Growth
79	
80	CRDT state grows monotonically (especially G-Set). Need a compaction/garbage-collection strategy for long-lived inboxes.
81	
82	## Relationship to Existing Work
83	
84	- **IPNS resolution alternatives todo:** Solving resolution reliability is a prerequisite. Self-hosted IPNS or improved caching directly benefits this approach.
85	- **Phase 14 trade-offs:** This is a third option beyond "server-side records" and "metadata-embedded ACLs" — a decentralized discovery layer that keeps metadata schemas clean.
86	- **Move rootFolderKey to IPFS todo:** Same philosophical direction — reducing server-side state.
87	
88	## Success Criteria
89	
90	- Identify a CRDT data structure suitable for share invitations (likely G-Set or OR-Set)
91	- Prototype write-conflict resolution: two concurrent IPNS publishes to the same inbox merge correctly on read
92	- Evaluate whether the write-access-control problem is solvable without reintroducing a centralized component
93	- Determine if this pattern generalizes to folder metadata sync (the bigger win)
94	- Assess IPNS publish/resolve latency impact of CRDT-encoded content vs current approach
95	
```

4	area: shares

10	
11	## Problem
12	
13	Security finding **M1** from `REVIEW-2026-02-21-phase14.md`, still **open** as of 2026-06-13 (verified against live code). The shares table stores `itemName` (file/folder names) as server-readable plaintext, leaking content metadata for shared items even though the server is otherwise zero-knowledge.
14	
15	Evidence:
16	
17	- `apps/api/src/shares/entities/share.entity.ts:45-50` — `itemName` is a plaintext `varchar(255)` (the column comment explicitly notes it is plaintext).
18	- `apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts:96` — server stores the raw `dto.itemName`.
19	- `apps/web/src/services/share.service.ts:117` — client sends the raw name. Contrast: `encryptedKey` in the same flow IS ECIES-wrapped, so the pattern exists.
20	
21	This was previously bundled in `.planning/todos/done/2026-02-21-phase14-security-review-deferred.md` (M1, M5, L1, L4). M5, L1, and L4 have since been implemented, so that todo was closed — but M1 was never addressed and fell off the actionable queue. This todo re-surfaces it.
22	
23	## Solution
24	
25	Encrypt `itemName` with the recipient's public key (ECIES), mirroring the `encryptedKey` flow, and decrypt client-side for display:
26	
27	- Add an encrypted column (longer field for ciphertext) on the shares entity; migrate the plaintext column.
28	- API stores only the ciphertext; no plaintext name is persisted.
29	- Client encrypts the name with the recipient pubkey on share creation and decrypts on render.
30	
31	Note: M1 is documented in `REVIEW-2026-02-21-phase14.md` as an accepted trade-off for the share-discovery UX. Confirm whether to implement or formally accept-and-document before scheduling.
32

> AGENT

Read all four. Both groupings are real, but they're different *kinds* of relationship — one is "do together," the other is "one supersedes the other."

## Cluster A — #8 + #9: finish moving folder-state ownership into the SDK

These genuinely belong on one branch (#9 already cross-links #8: *"Both move state authority into the SDK"*). But they're asymmetric in size and risk:

- **#9 (low, cleanup):** delete the ~16 web `ensureFolderRegistered` seeders + the duplicate web-side key-unwrap in `useFolderNavigation`, now redundant after #498's self-bootstrap. ⚠️ It's explicitly gated: *"once self-bootstrap has proven out in staging/prod."* #498 landed **today** (commit `2657740f1`) — so deleting the safety-net seeding now means removing the fallback before #498 has cleared staging. Verify that first.
- **#8 (medium, multi-PR):** teach the SDK to own *shared*-folder state and route `useSharedWriteOps` through it — the shared-folder counterpart to #494's owned-folder work. This is the real lift.

So: same through-line, one branch — but #9 is the quick win (pending the staging gate) and #8 is the substantive piece.

## Cluster B — #2 + #5: supersession, not co-execution

The connection is real but it's the opposite of "do together":

- **#5 (open MEDIUM, M1):** `shares.itemName` is plaintext server-side. Fix = ECIES-wrap it (mirroring `encryptedKey`), or formally accept-and-document.
- **#2 (research, long-horizon):** replace the centralized `shares` table with a serverless CRDT IPNS inbox. Because *all* inbox content is ECIES-wrapped to the recipient, the plaintext-`itemName` leak disappears for free — **#2 subsumes #5.**

The trap: #5 is a live security finding; #2 is research whose own success criteria are "prototype / evaluate / assess." You can't hold an open MEDIUM hostage to a quarters-out research idea. Right move is to **cross-link** (record in #2 that it subsumes M1/#5) and decide #5 on its own merits now — not bundle them.

---

These choices aren't mutually exclusive — pick any that apply.

## WEB-E2E FAILURE INVESTIGATION — run 27587113911 (CI E2E Tests / Web E2E Tests job)

### FAILING TEST(S)
1. `restores a subfolder item after reload without navigating into the subfolder`
   - Spec: `tests/web-e2e/tests/bin-restore-after-reload.spec.ts:78` (the brand-new test added **by #498 itself**)
2. `6.6.2 Restore a past version`
   - Spec: `tests/web-e2e/tests/full-workflow.spec.ts:1285`

(Also `6 did not run`, `173 passed`. 2 hard failures, `retries: 0`, `workers: 1`.)

### ERROR
**Test 1** — failed at **step 6 (item never reached the bin)**, not the restore step:
```
TimeoutError: locator.waitFor: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
  waiting for locator('[data-testid^="bin-item-"]')
  .filter({ hasText: 'reload-restore-1781572328631.txt' }) to be visible
  at bin.page.ts:80 (waitForBinItem)  ← called from bin-restore-after-reload.spec.ts:116
```
The deleted file never showed up in the recycle bin after delete+reload — so `deleteToBin` (which #498 modified) silently failed to land the entry, or the bin metadata wasn't published.

**Test 2** — version restore landed the wrong version:
```
expect(received).toBe(expected)
  Expected: "Updated content after edit - version 2"
  Received: "Edited in-browser via text editor modal - version 3"
  at full-workflow.spec.ts:1326
```
Restoring "past version 2" produced version-3 content — the folder/file pointer state was stale, so the restore operated on a stale snapshot.

### FAILED STEP
CI step **#12 "Run Web E2E tests"** (Playwright). All build/setup steps (1–11) passed, including "Build packages". This is a test-logic/runtime failure, not a build break.

### ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS — caused by #498, confidence: HIGH
This is **#498's self-bootstrap change**, not flake or pre-existing.

- #498 added `await this.requireFolder(folderIpnsName)` at the top of `deleteToBin` and `restoreFromBin`, and rerouted every folder mutation through `requireFolder` → `ensureFolderLoaded`.
- The defect: `ensureFolderLoaded` → `loadFolder` calls **`this.folderTree.set(ipnsName, state)` unconditionally** (client.ts:385). When self-bootstrap fires for a folder that is missing from `folderTree` (post-reload, or never-navigated this session), it resolves the folder from IPNS and **clobbers in-memory state with the IPNS-resolved snapshot**. IPNS reads are eventually-consistent / can lag a just-written sequence, so the snapshot is stale.
- **Test 1**: after delete+reload the subfolder isn't in folderTree; `deleteToBin` now self-bootstraps it, then `addToBin` publishes the parent on top of that snapshot — the bin entry / parent republish ends up inconsistent and the item never surfaces in the bin (timeout at `waitForBinItem`). Notably this is the exact code path the test was written to exercise — and it fails before even reaching restore.
- **Test 2**: same clobber mechanism — the version-restore path routes through `requireFolder`, self-bootstrap overwrites the fresher in-memory file-pointer/folder state with a stale IPNS snapshot, so "restore version 2" resolves against stale data and yields version-3 content.

This matches the known **"Web/SDK folder-state desync"** class (PR #489 memory): treat IPNS `sequenceNumber` as the version clock; `loadFolder` must not blindly overwrite a fresher in-memory entry with a stale resolve.

Lower-probability contributor (worth a glance, not the prime suspect): `ensureFolderLoaded` loads children with `publicKey: new Uint8Array(0)` (publicKey derived at sign time) — sub-agent confirmed signing derives from the private key, so this is likely benign.

### PRE-#498 STATUS
**Green.** The immediately preceding main-push CI-E2E run — `898fbdc51` (the commit right before #498), run `27584831708` — was **success**. `bin-restore-after-reload.spec.ts` did not exist before #498 (it's net-new in the commit), and `full-workflow.spec.ts:6.6.2` was passing on the prior green run. #498 is the regressing change.

### RELEVANT FILES
- `packages/sdk/src/client.ts`
  - `loadFolder` ~line 361–385 — the unconditional `folderTree.set()` at ~385 is the core bug (overwrites fresher state).
  - `ensureFolderLoaded` ~line 396–470 (added by #498).
  - `requireFolder` ~line 500 (added by #498).
  - `deleteToBin` ~line 1670 — new `await this.requireFolder(folderIpnsName)` at ~1675.
  - `restoreFromBin` ~line 1711 — new `await this.requireFolder(targetFolderIpnsName, 'Target folder')` at ~1718.
- `tests/web-e2e/tests/bin-restore-after-reload.spec.ts:78` (failing assertion path at :116, via `page-objects/pages/bin.page.ts:80`).
- `tests/web-e2e/tests/full-workflow.spec.ts:1326`.

### FIX DIRECTION
Make self-bootstrap non-clobbering: in `loadFolder` (or before its `folderTree.set`), if an entry already exists, keep the higher IPNS `sequenceNumber` (reconcile rather than blindly overwrite) — and have `ensureFolderLoaded` skip re-loading folders already present. The bin paths should self-heal only the *missing* folder, never re-resolve and overwrite already-loaded state, so `addToBin`/`restoreFromBin` publish on top of the freshest local snapshot. This is the same `sequenceNumber`-as-version-clock reconciliation pattern established in PR #489.

### Phase 46: Desktop FUSE data-loss bugs + replay hardening

**Goal:** Close the desktop FUSE write-durability work that Phase 45 explicitly deferred — the three known data-loss bugs (mkdir orphan on parent-publish conflict, release() false-durability ack, stale-mount recovery on crash), the two replay-path hardening follow-ups from PR #491, and the remaining read_ops/write_ops + journal_helpers test coverage (Phase 45 Tier 2). Behavior-changing: these are correctness/durability fixes, not hygiene.
**Requirements:** (1) mkdir must durably retry the parent publish on conflict instead of warn-only, so the new child folder is never orphaned remotely; (2) release()/flush must not ack the OS or zeroize+delete the local temp file until the remote commit is durably confirmed or the write is journaled for replay; (3) Linux startup must auto-recover a stale/disconnected FUSE mount (EEXIST/ENOTCONN) instead of failing and notifying; (4) park legacy empty `file_meta_ipns_name` replay entries instead of publishing an empty FilePointer; (5) use a strict (cache-bypassing) IPNS resolve in replay classification so transient failures retain the entry; (6) add the read_ops/write_ops handler test harness (unblock the fuser `ReplySender` limitation) plus the `journal_helpers` builder tests. Preserve all existing crash-recovery semantics.
**Depends on:** Phase 45
**Plans:** 4 plans

Plans:

- [ ] 46-01-PLAN.md — REQ-6 test harness: vendored `ReplySender` export + `make_test_fs` + `CaptureSender` + journal_helpers builder tests (Wave 1, lands first)
- [ ] 46-02-PLAN.md — REQ-3 Linux stale-mount recovery: `recover_stale_mount` + mountinfo parser + EEXIST retry (Wave 2)
- [ ] 46-03-PLAN.md — REQ-4 park legacy empty-name replay entries + REQ-5 strict cache-bypassing replay resolve (Wave 2)
- [ ] 46-04-PLAN.md — REQ-1/REQ-2 mkdir + release durability characterization tests + Open Question A2 verification (Wave 3, tests-only)

### Phase 47: SDK folder-state and publish-path consolidation

**Goal:** Pay down the Phase-44 SDK structural debt surfaced by `/simplify` and `/code-review` — one owner for folder state, one CAS-retry engine shared by file and folder publishes, encapsulated child bookkeeping, and the `prunedCids` pin-leak fix on the shared-file path. Mostly refactor, plus one correctness fix (pin leak).
**Requirements:** (1) Unify folder-state ownership so the web Zustand `useFolderStore` and the SDK client `folderTree` can no longer drift — make the SDK client the single source of truth: route the two leaking web file hooks (`useFileOperations.updateFile`, `useFileVersions` restore/delete) through new SDK client methods that own publish + sequence bookkeeping + `folder:updated` emission, make `useFolderStore` a projection whose `children`/`sequenceNumber` are written only via `folder:updated` events (never from web mutation code), and delete the `reconcileFolderState` band-aid (dead by construction, closing the residual race). Scope is folder-state-*mutating* paths only — non-mutating sdk-core usage in the web app (crypto, uploads, metadata fetch/decrypt) stays. (2) unify the duplicated file/folder 409-CAS-retry loops into one `publishWithCas` helper in sdk-core so retry/backoff/sequence handling lives in one place; (3) encapsulate the `baseChildren`/`publishedChildren` snapshot-and-adopt ceremony inside `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` so the ~14 call sites can't forget the base snapshot and resurrect deletes; (4) consume `prunedCids` in `updateSharedFile` and unpin them to stop the shared-file storage pin leak.

Confirmed — and you're right, manual dispatch is the mechanism. Here's the precise picture:

- **`ci-e2e.yml`** is the auto path: `push: branches: [main]` → paths-filter → calls web-e2e via `workflow_call`. That's the main-only auto-trigger (and the gap that let #498 land unverified).
- **`web-e2e.yml`** is directly `workflow_dispatch`-enabled and checks out `ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`. On a dispatch against a branch, `github.sha` = that branch's HEAD.

So **no CI change is needed** — the moment the fix branch is pushed:

```
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh workflow run web-e2e.yml --ref <fix-branch>
```

runs the identical Web E2E job against the branch's code, pre-merge. (Direct dispatch resolves repo secrets directly, so it faithfully reproduces the main-push run — no `secrets: inherit` parent needed.)

The thing to actually *ensure* is procedural: make this the **pre-merge acceptance gate for REQ-1**, so we never again confirm a folderTree fix only via the post-merge main run. Let me bake that into the phase and record the dispatch escape-hatch in memory so it isn't re-lost.

87	## 1.5. Closed-Phase Gate (#3569)
88	
89	The init JSON includes `phase_status` — one of `Pending | Planned | In Progress | Executed | Complete | Needs Review`. `Complete` means the phase has all summaries AND a `VERIFICATION.md` with `status: passed`. Replanning a closed phase silently rewrites plan docs that no longer match the shipped code, so the workflow must hard-stop here unless the operator explicitly overrides.
90	
91	Parse `phase_status` from the init JSON, then:
92	
93	```bash
94	FORCE_REPLAN=false
95	if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--force([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then
96	  FORCE_REPLAN=true
97	fi
98	
99	if [ "${phase_status}" = "Complete" ]; then
100	  if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--reviews([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then
101	    # --reviews on a closed phase is never legitimate — concerns belong in a
102	    # new phase or issue against the closed phase's commits.
103	    cat <<EOF >&2
104	Phase ${phase_number} (${phase_name}) is already CLOSED (VERIFICATION status: passed).
105	/gsd-plan-phase --reviews cannot replan a closed phase. If the review surfaced
106	real concerns, open a follow-up phase or file an issue against the closed
107	phase's commits. There is no --force override for --reviews on a closed phase.
108	EOF
109	    exit 1
110	  fi
111	  if [ "$FORCE_REPLAN" != "true" ]; then
112	    cat <<EOF >&2
113	Phase ${phase_number} (${phase_name}) is already CLOSED (VERIFICATION status: passed).
114	Replanning a closed phase will overwrite plan docs that no longer match the
115	shipped code. If you intentionally want to replan over closed work, re-run
116	with: /gsd-plan-phase ${phase_number} --force
117	
118	Otherwise, to view what shipped, see: ${verification_path}
119	EOF
120	    exit 1
121	  fi
122	  # FORCE_REPLAN=true: continue, but emit a banner so the operator sees the
123	  # decision in the transcript and in any committed plan docs.
124	  echo "WARNING: Replanning CLOSED phase ${phase_number} under --force. Verify the closeout was wrong before committing new plan docs." >&2
125	fi
126	```
127	
128	The gate fires only on `Complete`. `Executed` and `Needs Review` are not gated — those states mean planning was finished but verification did not pass, and replanning is a legitimate next step.

Use this for cross-phase research, doc review before committing to a planning approach, and correction-without-replanning loops. Replaces the deleted `/gsd-research-phase` command.

136	In research-only mode, two modifiers control behavior when `RESEARCH.md` already exists:

473	## 5. Handle Research
474	
475	**Skip if:** `--gaps` flag or `--skip-research` flag or `--reviews` flag.
476	
477	### 5.0. Research-Only Modifiers (`--view`, `--research`)
478	
479	**Skip if:** `RESEARCH_ONLY` is `false`.
480	
481	Three branches in research-only mode (`--research-phase <N>`):
482	
483	1. **`--view`**: print `RESEARCH.md` to stdout, no spawn, exit. If `RESEARCH.md` is missing, error with: `--view requires an existing RESEARCH.md; drop --view to spawn the researcher.`
484	2. **`--research`** (force-refresh): re-spawn researcher unconditionally — fall through to "Spawn gsd-phase-researcher" below.
485	3. **Neither flag AND `has_research=true`:** auto-use the existing research and exit cleanly — do not prompt, do not re-spawn. Emit `RESEARCH.md already exists for Phase ${PHASE}, using it. To force-refresh, re-invoke with --research; to print, re-invoke with --view. Path: ${research_path}` then exit. The explicit-flag escape hatches cover any deviation; this matches §5.1's promptless auto-use of existing research, removing the §5.0/§5.1 inconsistency (#159).
486	
487	```bash
488	if [[ "$VIEW_ONLY" == "true" ]]; then
489	  [[ -f "$research_path" ]] || { echo "Error: --view requires an existing RESEARCH.md (Phase ${PHASE}). Drop --view to spawn the researcher."; exit 1; }
490	  cat "$research_path"; exit 0
491	fi
492	```
493	
494	### 5.1. Standard Research Decision
495	
496	**Skip if** `RESEARCH_ONLY=true` (the research-only mode in 5.0 already determined the path: spawn or exit). Without this guard, an LLM following the workflow could fall through into "use existing, skip to step 6" → planner spawn, violating the research-only contract. **CR #3045 finding: this gate makes the early-exit unreachable from any non-research-only branch.**
497	
498	**If `has_research` is true (from init) AND no `--research` flag:** Use existing, skip to step 6.
499	
500	**If RESEARCH.md missing OR `--research` flag:**

527	    ]

542

This prevents duplicate work, conflicting edits, and wasted context. Only resume when the subagent result is available.

754	## 5.7. Schema Push Detection Gate
755	
756	> Detects schema-relevant files in the phase scope and injects a mandatory `[BLOCKING]` schema push task into the plan. Prevents false-positive verification where build/types pass because TypeScript types come from config, not the live database.
757	
758	Check if any files in the phase scope match schema patterns:
759	
760	```bash
761	PHASE_SECTION=$(gsd_run query roadmap.get-phase "${PHASE}" --pick section 2>/dev/null)
762	```
763	
764	Scan `PHASE_SECTION`, `CONTEXT.md` (if loaded), and `RESEARCH.md` (if exists) for file paths matching these ORM patterns:
765	
766	| ORM         | File Patterns                                           |
767	| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
768	| Payload CMS | `src/collections/**/*.ts`, `src/globals/**/*.ts`        |
769	| Prisma      | `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/schema/*.prisma`        |
770	| Drizzle     | `drizzle/schema.ts`, `src/db/schema.ts`, `drizzle/*.ts` |
771	| Supabase    | `supabase/migrations/*.sql`                             |
772	| TypeORM     | `src/entities/**/*.ts`, `src/migrations/**/*.ts`        |
773	
774	Also check if any existing PLAN.md files for this phase already reference these file patterns in `files_modified`.
775	
776	**If schema-relevant files detected:**
777	
778	Set `SCHEMA_PUSH_REQUIRED=true` and `SCHEMA_ORM={detected_orm}`.
779	
780	Determine the push command for the detected ORM:
781	
782	| ORM         | Push Command                | Non-TTY Workaround                                       |
783	| ----------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
784	| Payload CMS | `npx payload migrate`       | `CI=true PAYLOAD_MIGRATING=true npx payload migrate`     |
785	| Prisma      | `npx prisma db push`        | `npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss` (if destructive) |
786	| Drizzle     | `npx drizzle-kit push`      | `npx drizzle-kit push`                                   |
787	| Supabase    | `supabase db push`          | Set `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` env var                      |
788	| TypeORM     | `npx typeorm migration:run` | `npx typeorm migration:run -d src/data-source.ts`        |
789	
790	Inject the following into the planner prompt (step 8) as an additional constraint:
791	
792	```markdown
793	<schema_push_requirement>
794	**[BLOCKING] Schema Push Required**
795	
796	This phase modifies schema-relevant files ({detected_files}). The planner MUST include
797	a `[BLOCKING]` task that runs the database schema push command AFTER all schema file
798	modifications are complete but BEFORE verification.
799	
800	- ORM detected: {SCHEMA_ORM}
801	- Push command: {push_command}
802	- Non-TTY workaround: {env_hint}
803	- If push requires interactive prompts that cannot be suppressed, flag the task for
804	  manual intervention with `autonomous: false`
805	
806	This task is mandatory — the phase CANNOT pass verification without it. Build and
807	type checks will pass without the push (types come from config, not the live database),
808	creating a false-positive verification state.
809	</schema_push_requirement>
810	```
811	
812	Display: `Schema files detected ({SCHEMA_ORM}) — [BLOCKING] push task will be injected into plans`

814	**If no schema-relevant files detected:** Skip silently to step 6.

The plan-review-convergence source-grounding pass reads this section to exclude newly-created symbols from drift verification; omitting it causes new symbols to be flagged for acknowledgement.

1037	<deep_work_rules>
1038	
1039	## Anti-Shallow Execution Rules (MANDATORY)
1040	
1041	Every task MUST include these fields — they are NOT optional:
1042	
1043	1. **`<read_first>`** — Files the executor MUST read before touching anything. Always include:
1044	   - The file being modified (so executor sees current state, not assumptions)
1045	   - Any "source of truth" file referenced in CONTEXT.md (reference implementations, existing patterns, config files, schemas)
1046	   - Any file whose patterns, signatures, types, or conventions must be replicated or respected
1047	
1048	2. **`<acceptance_criteria>`** — Verifiable conditions that prove the task was done correctly. Rules:
1049	   - Every criterion must be checkable as a source assertion, behavior assertion, test command, or CLI output
1050	   - NEVER use subjective language ("looks correct", "properly configured", "consistent with")
1051	   - Include exact strings, patterns, values, command outputs, or observable behavior where that is the right proof
1052	   - Examples:
1053	     - Code: `auth.py contains def verify_token(` / `test_auth.py exits 0`
1054	     - Behavior: `POST /api/auth/login returns 200 + httpOnly JWT cookie for valid credentials`
1055	     - Config: `.env.example contains DATABASE_URL=` / `Dockerfile contains HEALTHCHECK`
1056	     - Docs: `README.md contains '## Installation'` / `API.md lists all endpoints`
1057	     - Infra: `deploy.yml has rollback step` / `docker-compose.yml has healthcheck for db`
1058	
1059	3. **`<action>`** — Must include CONCRETE values, not references. Rules:
1060	   - NEVER say "align X with Y", "match X to Y", "update to be consistent" without specifying the exact target state
1061	   - Include concrete identifiers and reference values: config keys, function signatures, SQL table names, class names, import paths, env vars, endpoint paths, etc.
1062	   - If CONTEXT.md has a comparison table or expected values, copy only the target identifiers/values needed to remove ambiguity
1063	   - Do not include full file contents, fenced code blocks, or complete implementations in `<action>`
1064	   - The executor should understand the intended target state from `<action>` and use `<read_first>` files for current implementation details, patterns, and source-of-truth context
1065	
1066	**Why this matters:** Executor agents work from the plan text. Vague instructions like "update the config to match production" produce shallow one-line changes. Concrete instructions like "add DATABASE_URL, set POOL_SIZE=20, add REDIS_URL, and read config/runtime.ts before editing" produce complete work without turning the planner into the executor.
1067	</deep_work_rules>
1068

1075	- [ ] Every task has `<acceptance_criteria>` with behavior, test-command, CLI, or source assertions
1076	- [ ] Every `<action>` contains concrete identifiers without fenced code blocks or full implementations
1077	- [ ] Dependencies correctly identified

1080	- [ ] Every PLAN.md includes an "Artifacts this phase produces" section listing symbols created by this phase (decorators, classes, functions, CLI flags, struct/dataclass fields, new file paths)
1081	      </quality_gate>

1099	## 8.5. Chunked Planning Mode
1100	
1101	**Skip if `CHUNKED_MODE` is `false`.**
1102	
1103	Chunked mode splits the single long-lived planner Agent run into a short outline Agent run followed by
1104	N short per-plan Agent runs. Each run is bounded to ~3–5 min; each plan is committed individually
1105	for crash resilience. If any run hangs and the terminal is force-killed, rerunning
1106	`/gsd-plan-phase {N} --chunked` resumes from the last successfully committed plan.
1107	
1108	**Intended for new or in-progress chunked runs.** To recover plans already written by a prior
1109	_non-chunked_ run, use step 6's "Add more plans" or proceed directly to `/gsd-execute-phase`
1110	— don't start a fresh chunked run over existing non-chunked plans.
1111	
1112	### 8.5.1 Outline Phase (outline-only mode, ~2 min)
1113	
1114	**Resume detection:** If `${PHASE_DIR}/${PADDED_PHASE}-PLAN-OUTLINE.md` already exists **and
1115	is valid** (contains the `## OUTLINE COMPLETE` marker), skip this sub-step — the outline
1116	already exists from a previous run. Proceed directly to 8.5.2.
1117	
1118	```bash
1119	OUTLINE_FILE="${PHASE_DIR}/${PADDED_PHASE}-PLAN-OUTLINE.md"
1120	if [[ -f "$OUTLINE_FILE" ]] && grep -q "^## OUTLINE COMPLETE" "$OUTLINE_FILE"; then
1121	  # reuse existing outline — skip to 8.5.2
1122	fi
1123	```
1124	
1125	Display:
1126	
1127	```text
1128	◆ Chunked mode: spawning outline planner... (runs in a subagent — no output until it returns, ~1–5 min; expected, not a freeze)
1129	```
1130	
1131	Spawn the planner in **outline-only** mode — it must write only the outline manifest, not any
1132	PLAN.md files:

1144	
1145	  Return: ## OUTLINE COMPLETE with plan count.",

This prevents duplicate work, conflicting edits, and wasted context. Only resume when the subagent result is available.

1211	## 9. Handle Planner Return
1212	
1213	- **`## PLANNING COMPLETE`:** Display plan count. If `--skip-verify` or `plan_checker_enabled` is false (from init): skip to step 13. Otherwise: step 10.
1214	- **`## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED`:** The planner determined the phase exceeds the context budget for full-fidelity implementation of all source items. Handle in step 9b.
1215	- **`## ⚠ Source Audit: Unplanned Items Found`:** The planner's multi-source coverage audit found items from REQUIREMENTS.md, RESEARCH.md, ROADMAP goal, or CONTEXT.md decisions that are not covered by any plan. Handle in step 9c.
1216	- **`## CHECKPOINT REACHED`:** Present to user, get response, spawn continuation (step 12)
1217	- **`## PLANNING INCONCLUSIVE`:** Show attempts, offer: Add context / Retry / Manual
1218	- **Empty / truncated / no recognized marker:** → Filesystem fallback (step 9a).
1219	
1220	## 9a. Filesystem Fallback (Planner)
1221	
1222	**Triggered when:** Agent() returns but the return contains no recognized marker (`## PLANNING COMPLETE`, `## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED`, `## ⚠ Source Audit`, `## CHECKPOINT REACHED`, `## PLANNING INCONCLUSIVE`).
1223	
1224	```bash
1225	DISK_PLANS=$(ls "${PHASE_DIR}"/*-PLAN.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
1226	```
1227	
1228	**If `DISK_PLANS` > 0:** The planner wrote plans to disk but the Agent() return was empty or
1229	truncated (the Windows stdio hang pattern — the subagent finished but the return never
1230	arrived). Display:
1231	
1232	```text
1233	◆ Planner wrote {DISK_PLANS} plan(s) to disk but did not emit a PLANNING COMPLETE marker.
1234	  This is a known Windows stdio hang pattern — work is likely recoverable.
1235	
1236	  Plans found on disk:
1237	  {ls output of *-PLAN.md}
1238	```
1239	
1240	Offer 3 options:
1241	
1242	1. **Accept plans** — treat as `## PLANNING COMPLETE` and continue through step 9 `## PLANNING COMPLETE` handling (so `--skip-verify` / `plan_checker_enabled=false` are honored — may skip to step 13 rather than step 10)
1243	2. **Retry planner** — re-spawn the planner with the same prompt (return to step 8)
1244	3. **Stop** — exit; user can re-run `/gsd-plan-phase {N}` to resume
1245	
1246	**If `DISK_PLANS` is 0 and no marker:** The planner produced no output. Treat as
1247	`## PLANNING INCONCLUSIVE` and handle accordingly.
1248	
1249	## 9b. Handle Phase Split Recommendation
1250	
1251	When the planner returns `## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED`, it means the phase's source items exceed the context budget for full-fidelity implementation. The planner proposes groupings.
1252	
1253	**Extract from planner return:**
1254	
1255	- Proposed sub-phases (e.g., "17a: processing core (D-01 to D-19)", "17b: billing + config UX (D-20 to D-27)")
1256	- Which source items (REQ-IDs, D-XX decisions, RESEARCH items) go in each sub-phase
1257	- Why the split is necessary (context cost estimate, file count)
1258	
1259	**Present to user:**
1260	
1261	```
1262	## Phase {X} exceeds context budget for full-fidelity implementation
1263	
1264	The planner found {N} source items that exceed the context budget when
1265	planned at full fidelity. Instead of reducing scope, we recommend splitting:
1266	
1267	**Option 1: Split into sub-phases**
1268	- Phase {X}a: {name} — {items} ({N} source items, ~{P}% context)
1269	- Phase {X}b: {name} — {items} ({M} source items, ~{Q}% context)
1270	
1271	**Option 2: Proceed anyway** (planner will attempt all, quality may degrade past 50% context)
1272	
1273	**Option 3: Prioritize** — you choose which items to implement now,
1274	rest become a follow-up phase
1275	```
1276	
1277	Use AskUserQuestion with these 3 options.
1278	
1279	**If "Split":** Use `/gsd-phase --insert` to create the sub-phases, then replan each.
1280	**If "Proceed":** Return to planner with instruction to attempt all items at full fidelity, accepting more plans/tasks.
1281	**If "Prioritize":** Use AskUserQuestion (multiSelect) to let user pick which items are "now" vs "later". Create CONTEXT.md for each sub-phase with the selected items.
1282	
1283	## 9c. Handle Source Audit Gaps
1284	
1285	When the planner returns `## ⚠ Source Audit: Unplanned Items Found`, it means items from REQUIREMENTS.md, RESEARCH.md, ROADMAP goal, or CONTEXT.md decisions have no corresponding plan.
1286	
1287	**Extract from planner return:**
1288	
1289	- Each unplanned item with its source artifact and section
1290	- The planner's suggested options (A: add plan, B: split phase, C: defer with confirmation)
1291	
1292	**Present each gap to user.** For each unplanned item:
1293	
1294	```
1295	## ⚠ Unplanned: {item description}
1296	
1297	Source: {RESEARCH.md / REQUIREMENTS.md / ROADMAP goal / CONTEXT.md}
1298	Details: {why the planner flagged this}
1299	
1300	Options:
1301	1. Add a plan to cover this item (recommended)
1302	2. Split phase — move to a sub-phase with related items
1303	3. Defer — add to backlog (developer confirms this is intentional)
1304	```
1305	
1306	Use AskUserQuestion for each gap (or batch if multiple gaps).
1307	
1308	**If "Add plan":** Return to planner (step 8) with instruction to add plans covering the missing items, preserving existing plans.
1309	**If "Split":** Use `/gsd-phase --insert` for overflow items, then replan.
1310	**If "Defer":** Record in CONTEXT.md `## Deferred Ideas` with developer's confirmation. Proceed to step 10.

1415	## 12. Revision Loop (Max 3 Iterations)
1416	
1417	Track `iteration_count` (starts at 1 after initial plan + check).
1418	Track `prev_issue_count` (initialized to `Infinity` before the loop begins).
1419	Track `stall_reentry_count` (starts at 0; incremented each time "Adjust approach" re-enters step 8).

1421	**If iteration_count < 3:**
1422	
1423	Parse issue count from checker return: count BLOCKER + WARNING entries in the YAML issues block (structured output from gsd-plan-checker). If the checker's return contains no YAML issues block (i.e., the plan was approved with no issues), treat `issue_count` as 0 and skip the stall check — the plan passed. Proceed to step 13.
1424	
1425	Display: `Revision iteration {N}/3 -- {blocker_count} blockers, {warning_count} warnings`
1426	
1427	**Stall detection:** If `issue_count >= prev_issue_count`:
1428	Display: `Revision loop stalled — issue count not decreasing ({issue_count} issues remain after {N} iterations)`
1429	
1430	**If `stall_reentry_count < 2`:**
1431	Ask user:
1432	Question: "Issues remain after {N} revision attempts with no progress. Proceed with current output?"
1433	Options: "Proceed anyway" | "Adjust approach"
1434	If "Proceed anyway": accept current plans and continue to step 13.
1435	If "Adjust approach": increment `stall_reentry_count`, open freeform discussion, then re-enter step 8 (full replanning). Note: re-entry resets `iteration_count` and `prev_issue_count` but `stall_reentry_count` persists across re-entries and is capped at 2.
1436	
1437	**If `stall_reentry_count >= 2`:**
1438	Display: `Stall persists after 2 re-planning attempts. The following issues could not be resolved automatically:`
1439	List the remaining issues from the checker.
1440	Suggest: "Consider resolving these issues manually or running `/gsd-debug` to investigate root causes."
1441	Options: "Proceed anyway" | "Abandon"
1442	If "Proceed anyway": accept current plans and continue to step 13.
1443	If "Abandon": stop workflow.

1491	## 12.5. Plan Bounce (Optional External Refinement)

111	Codex maps subagents to `spawn_agent`, which has no direct Codex mapping for Claude Code's `isolation="worktree"` parameter. Failing closed prevents main-checkout edits while the workflow believes agents are isolated.
112	
113	If the project uses git submodules, worktree isolation is unsafe **only when a plan touches a submodule path** — the executor commit protocol cannot correctly handle submodule commits inside isolated worktrees. The previous behavior unconditionally disabled worktree isolation whenever `.gitmodules` existed, which penalised every plan in a submodule project even when the plan was nowhere near a submodule. Compute submodule paths once and intersect them per-plan with the plan's declared `files_modified` frontmatter.
114	
115	```bash
116	# Parse submodule paths from .gitmodules once (empty if no .gitmodules).
117	# SUBMODULE_PATHS is a newline-separated list of repo-relative paths.
118	if [ -f .gitmodules ]; then
119	  SUBMODULE_PATHS=$(git config --file .gitmodules --get-regexp '^submodule\..*\.path$' 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}')
120	else
121	  SUBMODULE_PATHS=""
122	fi
123	```
124	
125	`SUBMODULE_PATHS` is exported to the `execute_waves` step, where the per-plan decision actually happens (see "Per-plan worktree decision" sub-step inside `execute_waves`). The decision is per-plan because different plans in the same wave can touch different files — only plans whose paths intersect a submodule must drop worktree isolation; plans nowhere near a submodule keep parallel isolation.
126	
127	When `USE_WORKTREES` (project-level) is `false`, all executor agents run without `isolation="worktree"` — they execute sequentially on the main working tree instead of in parallel worktrees. The per-plan decision below has no effect when worktrees are project-disabled.
128	
129	`USE_WORKTREES` is also automatically set to `false` for the duration of a run when `worktree base-check` detects that the orchestrator HEAD has diverged from the worktree fork base (the #683 condition — e.g. an unmerged milestone or feature branch). This check runs only when `RUNTIME=claude` because `isolation="worktree"` is a Claude Code-specific feature; other runtimes do not use it. The auto-degrade prints a one-line warning to stderr and falls through to the sequential path so executors do not hit the exit-42 worktree-branch-check halt. To restore parallel worktree execution, set `worktree.baseRef:"head"` in `.claude/settings.local.json` (or run `gsd-tools worktree set-baseref`) — this makes the fork base track the live HEAD instead of a fixed remote ref. The `worktree-branch-check` exit-42 guard inside each executor remains in place as a backstop.

241	<step name="check_interactive_mode">
242	**Parse `--interactive` flag from $ARGUMENTS.**
243	
244	**If `--interactive` flag present:** Switch to interactive execution mode.
245	
246	Interactive mode executes plans sequentially **inline** (no subagent spawning) with user
247	checkpoints between tasks. The user can review, modify, or redirect work at any point.
248	
249	**Interactive execution flow:**
250	
251	1. Load plan inventory as normal (discover_and_group_plans)
252	2. For each plan (sequentially, ignoring wave grouping):
253	
254	   a. **Present the plan to the user:**
255	
256	   ```
257	   ## Plan {plan_id}: {plan_name}
258	
259	   Objective: {from plan file}
260	   Tasks: {task_count}
261	
262	   Options:
263	   - Execute (proceed with all tasks)
264	   - Review first (show task breakdown before starting)
265	   - Skip (move to next plan)
266	   - Stop (end execution, save progress)
267	   ```
268	
269	   b. **If "Review first":** Read and display the full plan file. Ask again: Execute, Modify, Skip.
270	
271	   c. **If "Execute":** Read and follow `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/gsd-core/workflows/execute-plan.md` **inline**
272	   (do NOT spawn a subagent). Execute tasks one at a time.
273	
274	   d. **After each task:** Pause briefly. If the user intervenes (types anything), stop and address
275	   their feedback before continuing. Otherwise proceed to next task.
276	
277	   e. **After plan complete:** Show results, commit, create SUMMARY.md, then present next plan.
278	
279	3. After all plans: proceed to verification (same as normal mode).
280	
281	**Benefits of interactive mode:**
282	
283	- No subagent overhead — dramatically lower token usage
284	- User catches mistakes early — saves costly verification cycles
285	- Maintains GSD's planning/tracking structure
286	- Best for: small phases, bug fixes, verification gaps, learning GSD
287	
288	**Skip to handle_branching step** (interactive plans execute inline after grouping).
289	</step>

291	<step name="handle_branching">
292	Check `branching_strategy` from init:
293	
294	**"none":** Skip, continue on current branch.
295	
296	**"phase" or "milestone":** Use pre-computed `branch_name` from init.
297	
298	Fork the new phase branch off `origin/HEAD` (the project's default branch), not the current HEAD — otherwise consecutive phases compound and stay unpushed (#2916). If `$BRANCH_NAME` already exists locally, reuse it as-is.
299	
300	```bash
301	DEFAULT_BRANCH=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^origin/||')
302	DEFAULT_BRANCH=${DEFAULT_BRANCH:-main}
303	
304	if git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$BRANCH_NAME"; then
305	  git switch "$BRANCH_NAME" || { echo "ERROR: Could not switch to existing branch '$BRANCH_NAME'." >&2; exit 1; }
306	else
307	  if ! git fetch --quiet origin "$DEFAULT_BRANCH"; then  # #2916
308	    git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/remotes/origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH" \
309	      || { echo "ERROR: fetch origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH failed and no local copy exists. Refusing to create '$BRANCH_NAME' off current HEAD (#2916)." >&2; exit 1; }
310	    echo "WARNING: fetch origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH failed; using local copy as base." >&2
311	  fi
312	  if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
313	    echo "WARNING: Uncommitted changes will be carried onto '$BRANCH_NAME' (branched off origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH, not previous HEAD)."
314	  else
315	    git switch --quiet "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" 2>/dev/null && git merge --ff-only --quiet "origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
316	  fi
317	  # Pinned base + fail-fast: on success HEAD is exactly at origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH,
318	  # so a post-creation merge-base or "ahead-of" guard would be unreachable. The
319	  # explicit base argument here is the single source of correctness for #2916.
320	  git checkout -b "$BRANCH_NAME" "origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH" \
321	    || { echo "ERROR: Could not create '$BRANCH_NAME' from origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH (#2916)." >&2; exit 1; }
322	fi
323	```

325	All subsequent commits go to this branch. User handles merging.

374	<step name="cross_ai_delegation">
375	**Optional step 2.5 — Delegate plans to an external AI runtime.**
376	
377	This step runs after plan discovery and before normal wave execution. It identifies plans
378	that should be delegated to an external AI command and executes them via stdin-based prompt
379	delivery. Plans handled here are removed from the execute_waves plan list so the normal
380	executor skips them.
381	
382	**Activation logic:**
383	
384	1. If `CROSS_AI_DISABLED` is true (`--no-cross-ai` flag): skip this step entirely.
385	2. If `CROSS_AI_FORCE` is true (`--cross-ai` flag): mark ALL incomplete plans for cross-AI execution.
386	3. Otherwise: check each plan's frontmatter for `cross_ai: true` AND verify config
387	   `workflow.cross_ai_execution` is `true`. Plans matching both conditions are marked for cross-AI.
388	
389	```bash
390	CROSS_AI_ENABLED=$(gsd_run query config-get workflow.cross_ai_execution 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
391	CROSS_AI_CMD=$(gsd_run query config-get workflow.cross_ai_command 2>/dev/null || echo "")
392	CROSS_AI_TIMEOUT=$(gsd_run query config-get workflow.cross_ai_timeout 2>/dev/null || echo "300")
393	```
394	
395	**If no plans are marked for cross-AI:** Skip to execute_waves.
396	
397	**If plans are marked but `cross_ai_command` is empty:** Error — tell user to set
398	`workflow.cross_ai_command` via `gsd-tools.cjs query config-set workflow.cross_ai_command "<command>"`.
399	
400	**For each cross-AI plan (sequentially):**
401	
402	1. **Construct the task prompt** from the plan file:
403	   - Extract `<objective>` and `<tasks>` sections from the PLAN.md
404	   - Append PROJECT.md context (project name, description, tech stack)
405	   - Format as a self-contained execution prompt
406	
407	2. **Check for dirty working tree before execution:**
408	
409	   ```bash
410	   if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
411	     echo "WARNING: dirty working tree detected — the external AI command may produce uncommitted changes that conflict with existing modifications"
412	   fi
413	   ```
414	
415	3. **Run the external command** from the project root, writing the prompt to stdin.
416	   Never shell-interpolate the prompt — always pipe via stdin to prevent injection:
417	
418	   ```bash
419	   echo "$TASK_PROMPT" | timeout "${CROSS_AI_TIMEOUT}s" ${CROSS_AI_CMD} > "$CANDIDATE_SUMMARY" 2>"$ERROR_LOG"
420	   EXIT_CODE=$?
421	   ```
422	
423	4. **Evaluate the result:**
424	
425	   **Success (exit 0 + valid summary):**
426	   - Read `$CANDIDATE_SUMMARY` and validate it contains meaningful content
427	     (not empty, has at least a heading and description — a valid SUMMARY.md structure)
428	   - Write it as the plan's SUMMARY.md file
429	   - Update STATE.md plan status to complete
430	   - Update ROADMAP.md progress
431	   - Mark plan as handled — skip it in execute_waves
432	
433	   **Failure (non-zero exit or invalid summary):**
434	   - Display the error output and exit code
435	   - Warn: "The external command may have left uncommitted changes or partial edits
436	     in the working tree. Review `git status` and `git diff` before proceeding."
437	   - Offer three choices:
438	     - **retry** — run the same plan through cross-AI again
439	     - **skip** — fall back to normal executor for this plan (re-add to execute_waves list)
440	     - **abort** — stop execution entirely, preserve state for resume
441	
442	5. **After all cross-AI plans processed:** Remove successfully handled plans from the
443	   incomplete plan list so execute_waves skips them. Any skipped-to-fallback plans remain
444	   in the list for normal executor processing.
445	   </step>

447	<step name="execute_waves">
448	Execute each selected wave in sequence. Within a wave: parallel if `PARALLELIZATION=true`, sequential if `false`.
449	
450	**Orchestrator cwd-drift guard (FIRST ACTION at execute_waves entry — #48):**
451	
452	A prior `Agent(isolation="worktree")` dispatch can silently leave the orchestrator's
453	cwd inside an agent worktree (or a subdirectory of one). Every subsequent
454	orchestrator-side git call would then target the wrong tree — this is how a wrong-base
455	merge nearly shipped ~1000 files. Resolve the _worktree root_ (so a subdirectory cwd
456	cannot skew the check) and refuse if it is an agent worktree. The discriminator is the
457	per-agent branch namespace `worktree-agent-*`, NOT the `.claude/worktrees/` path: the
458	orchestrator may itself be legitimately invoked from a feature worktree under
459	`.claude/worktrees/`, so a path-substring refusal would break legitimate runs. Do NOT
460	pin to `git worktree list`'s first entry — that is the main worktree, the wrong target
461	when the orchestrator legitimately runs from a feature worktree.
462	
463	```bash
464	ORCHESTRATOR_WT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || {
465	  echo "FATAL: execute_waves entry is not inside a git worktree (#48)." >&2; exit 1; }
466	ORCH_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null)
467	if printf '%s' "$ORCH_BRANCH" | grep -Eq '^worktree-agent-'; then
468	  echo "FATAL: orchestrator cwd is inside an agent worktree (branch '$ORCH_BRANCH', root '$ORCHESTRATOR_WT') — refusing to execute waves (#48). A prior isolation=\"worktree\" dispatch drifted the cwd; re-run from the orchestrator's own worktree." >&2
469	  exit 1
470	fi
471	# Pin to the worktree root; each later orchestrator-side block re-pins the same way
472	# (see the #3174 cleanup guard). Treat $ORCHESTRATOR_WT as the canonical root for the
473	# rest of the phase — prefer `git -C "$ORCHESTRATOR_WT"` for cross-step git calls,
474	# since a bare `cd` does not persist across separate tool invocations.
475	export ORCHESTRATOR_WT
476	cd "$ORCHESTRATOR_WT" || { echo "FATAL: cannot cd to orchestrator worktree '$ORCHESTRATOR_WT' (#48)." >&2; exit 1; }
477	```
478	
479	**Stream-idle-timeout prevention — checkpoint heartbeats (#2410):**
480	
481	Multi-plan phases can accumulate enough subagent context that the Claude API
482	SSE layer terminates with `Stream idle timeout - partial response received`
483	between a large tool_result and the next assistant turn (seen on Claude Code
484	
485	- Opus 4.7 at ~200K+ cache_read). To keep the stream warm, emit short
486	  assistant-text heartbeats — **no tool call, just a literal line** — at every
487	  wave and plan boundary. Each heartbeat MUST start with `[checkpoint]` so
488	  tooling and `/gsd-manager`'s background-completion handler can grep partial
489	  transcripts. `{P}/{Q}` is the phase-wide completed/total plans counter and
490	  increases monotonically across waves. `{status}` is `complete` (success),
491	  `failed` (executor error), or `checkpoint` (human-gate returned).
492	
493	```
494	[checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} starting, {wave_plan_count} plan(s), {P}/{Q} plans done
495	[checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} plan {plan_id} starting ({P}/{Q} plans done)
496	[checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} plan {plan_id} {status} ({P}/{Q} plans done)
497	[checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} complete, {P}/{Q} plans done ({wave_success}/{wave_plan_count} ok)
498	```
499	
500	**For each wave:**
501	
502	1. **Intra-wave files_modified overlap check (BEFORE spawning):**
503	
504	   Before spawning any agents for this wave, inspect the `files_modified` list of all plans
505	   in the wave. Check every pair of plans in the wave — if any two plans share even one file
506	   in their `files_modified` lists, those plans have an implicit dependency and MUST NOT run
507	   in parallel.
508	
509	   **Detection algorithm (pseudocode):**
510	
511	   ```
512	   seen_files = {}
513	   overlapping_plans = []
514	   for each plan in wave_plans:
515	     for each file in plan.files_modified:
516	       if file in seen_files:
517	         overlapping_plans.add(plan, seen_files[file])  # both plans overlap on this file
518	       else:
519	         seen_files[file] = plan
520	   ```
521	
522	   **If overlap is detected:**
523	   - Warn the user:
524	     ```
525	     ⚠ Intra-wave files_modified overlap detected in Wave {N}:
526	       Plan {A} and Plan {B} both modify {file}
527	       Running these plans sequentially to avoid parallel worktree conflicts.
528	     ```
529	   - Override `PARALLELIZATION` to `false` for this wave only — run all plans in the wave
530	     sequentially regardless of the global parallelization setting.
531	   - This is a safety net for plans that were incorrectly assigned to the same wave.
532	     The planner should have caught this; flag it as a planning defect so the user can
533	     replan the phase if desired.
534	
535	   **If no overlap:** proceed normally (parallel if `PARALLELIZATION=true`).
536	
537	2. **Describe what's being built (BEFORE spawning):**
538	
539	   **First, emit the wave-start checkpoint heartbeat as a literal assistant-text
540	   line — no tool call (#2410). Do NOT skip this even for single-plan waves; it
541	   is required before any further reasoning or spawning:**
542	
543	   ```
544	   [checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} starting, {wave_plan_count} plan(s), {P}/{Q} plans done
545	   ```
546	
547	   Then read each plan's `<objective>`. Extract what's being built and why.
548	
549	   ```
550	   ---
551	   ## Wave {N}
552	
553	   **{Plan ID}: {Plan Name}**
554	   {2-3 sentences: what this builds, technical approach, why it matters}
555	
556	   Spawning {count} agent(s)... (runs in a subagent — no output until it returns, ~1–5 min; expected, not a freeze)
557	   ---
558	   ```
559	
560	   - Bad: "Executing terrain generation plan"
561	   - Good: "Procedural terrain generator using Perlin noise — creates height maps, biome zones, and collision meshes. Required before vehicle physics can interact with ground."
562	
563	2.5. **Per-plan worktree decision (run for each plan in this wave BEFORE its dispatch):**
564	
565	Read and execute `gsd-core/workflows/execute-phase/steps/per-plan-worktree-gate.md` for each plan. It extracts `PLAN_FILES` from the plan's JSON, intersects against `SUBMODULE_PATHS` (with normalization, bidirectional matching, and glob-prefix handling), and sets `USE_WORKTREES_FOR_PLAN` to `false` when the plan touches a submodule path. Append `plan_id` to a `WAVE_WORKTREE_PLANS` accumulator when `USE_WORKTREES_FOR_PLAN != false`.
566	
567	The dispatch branches in step 3 below MUST gate on `USE_WORKTREES_FOR_PLAN` for the current plan, not on the project-level `USE_WORKTREES`.

569	3. **Spawn executor agents:**
570	
571	   **Emit a plan-start heartbeat (literal line, no tool call) immediately before
572	   each `Agent()` dispatch (#2410):**
573	
574	   `[checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} plan {plan_id} starting ({P}/{Q} plans done)`

576	   Pass paths only — executors read files themselves with their fresh context window.
577	   For 200k models, this keeps orchestrator context lean (~10-15%).
578	   For 1M+ models (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6), richer context can be passed directly.
579	
580	   **Worktree mode** (`USE_WORKTREES_FOR_PLAN` is not `false` — evaluated per-plan in step 2.5):
581	
582	   Before spawning, capture the current HEAD:

584	   ```bash

586	   DISPATCH_TS=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
587	   EXPECTED_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
588	   if [ "${USE_WORKTREES_FOR_PLAN:-true}" != "false" ] && [ -z "${WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST:-}" ]; then

591	     # orchestrator's OWN worktree — NOT `git worktree list`'s first entry (always the main
592	     # checkout), which pins a non-primary (per-phase lane) orchestrator off its branch (#630).
593	     # Dispatch runs from the orchestrator's lane, so show-toplevel here is the correct root.

439	    // Cannot self-bootstrap without the root IPNS signing key.

457	    //    cycles in folder metadata.

The change is complete and correct. Here is my report.

## Report

### ROOT CAUSE
The failure is **not** a self-bootstrap / folder-not-loaded problem (the leading hypothesis is refuted). The bin list renders entirely from the bin entry itself (`BinListItem` reads `entry.name`/`entry.originalPath`), and `loadBin` is fully folder-independent — neither needs any subfolder loaded.

The real cause is a **destructive bin auto-repair on a transient resolve miss** in `packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts` `loadBin`. The code treated a `null` from `resolveIpnsRecord` as a definitive "bin is empty" signal and eagerly published an empty bin record. But `resolveIpnsRecord` also returns `null` on a cold-cache miss right after `page.reload()`, or while a concurrent `loadBin`/delete is mid-flight. After reload there are two concurrent `loadBin()` calls (login's fire-and-forget in `useAuth.ts:369` + `BinBrowser` mount).

Critically, the bin publish path passes **no `expectedSequenceNumber`**, and the API's `upsertFolderIpns` (`apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:226,244-246`) only runs its lower-sequence conflict guard when `expectedSequenceNumber` is provided — otherwise it **unconditionally increments the sequence and overwrites `latestCid`**. So a spurious empty-bin auto-repair doesn't just return empty in-memory; it can overwrite the real bin record's CID server-side, wiping the deleted item. Result: after reload the bin renders empty and `waitForBinItem` (step 6) times out, never reaching restore (step 7) — exactly why it failed earlier than the test author expected. I proved this with an in-memory IPNS+IPFS fake running the real bin code: the happy path passes, but a transient first-resolve null loses the entry pre-fix.

The integration test (`integration.test.ts` #143, root case) passes because it reuses one warm-cache session and never reloads.

### THE FIX
`packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts` (`loadBin`): make the auto-repair non-destructive.
- On the initial `null`, **re-resolve once** before assuming the bin is new; if a record surfaces (cold cache now warm / concurrent publish landed), adopt it and **skip the empty publish entirely** — no clobber.
- If still null, publish the empty bin, then **re-resolve after publishing**; if a real higher-sequence record now appears, return that instead of the empty state we just wrote.

SDK-only; no API/DTO changes, so no `pnpm api:generate` needed. The sequence guard in `client.ts:377-387` is untouched.

### TEST
`packages/sdk/src/__tests__/bin.test.ts`:
- New test `does NOT clobber a real record when the first resolve is a transient (cold-cache) null` — asserts the entry surfaces and **no** empty publish happens (`createAndPublishIpnsRecord`/`addToIpfs` not called).
- Updated the two existing auto-repair tests for the new re-resolve-before-publish call sequence.

`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk test`: **183 passed**. The only 3 failures are the pre-existing live-API `integration.test.ts` tests (no cipher-box API running locally — the process on :3000 is a different project; verified they fail identically with my change stashed; they're `describe.skip` in CI). All 11 bin tests pass; tsc + eslint clean.

### COMMIT
**Not committed.** The 1Password SSH signer is wedged (`error: 1Password: failed to fill whole buffer` on every attempt). Per project memory, recovery requires manually restarting the 1Password app, which I can't do autonomously, and I must not use `--no-gpg-sign` (PRs enforce signatures) or `--no-verify`. The two files are **staged and hook-formatted, ready to commit** once 1Password is restarted:

Suggested subject (no parens, commitlint-safe): `fix(48-01): re-resolve bin before auto-repair to prevent empty clobber`

### CONFIDENCE
**High** that this greens `bin-restore-after-reload.spec.ts`. The unit-level reproduction with faithful IPNS/IPFS fakes shows the exact pre-fix failure (entry lost on transient null) and post-fix recovery, and the fix also matches the live API's behavior (DB cache is written synchronously on publish, so the re-resolve reliably returns the real record). One residual: if step 4's delete itself never persisted a bin entry (e.g. `binState` still null at delete → `BinNotLoadedError` → hard-delete fallback in `useFolderMutations.ts:31`), this fix wouldn't help — but that path is unlikely given the seconds of UI work before the delete, and the auto-repair clobber is the mechanism that actually matches "item persisted then disappeared after reload."

> AGENT

**Decisive:** `BinBrowser`/`useBin` have **no** redirect logic at all. So the failure page (Files browser) means BinPage was mounted then the app navigated back to `/files`. The only thing that force-navigates to `/files` post-reload is the **auth/session-restore flow** — `useAuth.ts:465 navigate('/files')`. This is a **race**: the test treats `user-menu` visible (line 111) as "restored" and navigates to `/bin`, but the auth restore's final `navigate('/files')` fires *after* that, bouncing `/bin → /files`. That fits the screenshot exactly and explains why this brand-new test never passed. Confirming in `useAuth.ts`.

**Root cause found (high confidence) — and it's neither the SDK clobber nor the bin data.** It's a **navigation race in `useFolderNavigation`**:

- Step 4 deletes the file *while inside the subfolder*, so step 5 reloads at `/files/<subfolderId>`.
- After reload the subfolder isn't loaded; an async resolve of `<subfolderId>` runs with retries.
- `user-menu` appears → the test navigates to `/bin`.
- The subfolder resolve then fails/finishes and its catch block (`useFolderNavigation.ts:304-307`) calls `navigate('/files')` — guarded only by `latestNavTarget` (line 297), which a sidebar click to `/bin` doesn't update. So it **bounces `/bin → /files`**, and `waitForBinItem` times out on the files view. That's exactly the screenshot.

This is a real app bug (delete-in-subfolder → reload → open bin), low-risk to fix (guard the redirect so it doesn't fire when the user has navigated away). This is my final aimed attempt before parking. Delegating the minimal guard with a tight leash:

## Summary

ROOT-CAUSE CONFIRMED: Verified in `apps/web/src/hooks/useFolderNavigation.ts`. The async subfolder resolve in `navigateTo`'s `catch` (was lines 294-308) force-navigates to `/files` guarded ONLY by `if (latestNavTarget.current !== targetFolderId) return;`. A sidebar Bin click is a plain react-router nav (`/bin`), not `navigateTo`, so it never updates `latestNavTarget.current`. When the subfolder resolve then fails, the guard passes and the catch redirects the user off `/bin` back to `/files`, so the bin never renders and the test's `waitForBinItem` (step 6) times out. The `finally` block only clears `isLoading`; the success-path guards (lines 257, 291) don't navigate — the catch redirect is the sole offending navigation.

THE FIX (file: `apps/web/src/hooks/useFolderNavigation.ts`):
- Imported `useLocation` and added a `latestPathname` ref kept current via an effect on `location.pathname` (a ref is required because `navigateTo` is a `useCallback` with `[navigate]` deps, so a closure-captured `location` would be stale by the time the async catch runs).
- Added one guard line before the catch-block redirect: `if (latestPathname.current !== \`/files/${targetFolderId}\`) return;`

This is strictly fewer forced navigations. The existing `latestNavTarget` guard is unchanged. When the user is on `/bin` (or `/shared`/`/settings`), `latestPathname.current` is `/bin`, not `/files/<targetFolderId>`, so the redirect is skipped — matching the comment's stated intent (the redirect only exists to avoid a broken empty `/files/<uuid>` fallback, which doesn't apply once the user is off that route).

TEST / TYPECHECK / LINT:
- Typecheck `tsc -b`: PASS (exit 0).
- Lint `eslint src/hooks/useFolderNavigation.ts`: PASS (exit 0).
- Full web unit suite `vitest run`: 31/31 PASS — no regressions.
- No new unit test added. The hook is NOT cleanly unit-testable in this repo: `apps/web` has no `@testing-library/react`, no `renderHook`, no `react-test-renderer`, and no browser-mode vitest. Every existing `apps/web/src` test is a plain function/store test (`vi.mock` + direct calls); none render a React hook. Writing one would require either a hook renderer that doesn't exist or duplicating the inline guard expression in the test (which exercises nothing real). The guard is covered by the e2e spec it fixes.

You picked option 1 (land REQ-2 to fix the bounce) based on my earlier hypothesis. Before spending another 12-min CI cycle, I pulled the **Playwright trace** (the diagnostic I should have led with), and it overturns that hypothesis:

**Real root cause:** after the item is deleted to the bin and the page reloads, `loadBin`'s IPNS resolve 404s (propagation lag on the just-written bin record), and the destructive "auto-repair to empty" overwrites the real bin server-side. **What I'd otherwise have shipped wrongly:** REQ-2's deletion of the web seeding — irrelevant to this failure.

`loadBin` must never republish an empty bin on a *transient* 404 — it has to distinguish "bin never created" (safe to init empty) from "bin exists but momentarily unresolvable" (keep state / retry, never clobber). That likely needs the resolve API to disambiguate the two 404s (→ `pnpm api:generate`), and it's an IPNS-consistency change with real blast radius. Guessing at it via 12-min CI cycles is the wrong loop — it should be **reproduced locally** (the `tests/web-e2e` stack) where I can iterate in seconds.

> AGENT

This is the payoff — all three readers converge on a **clear, confirmed root cause and minimal fix**:

**Root cause:** `loadBin`'s auto-repair (`bin/index.ts:188-241`) **blind-publishes an empty bin** (no `expectedSequenceNumber`) on a double-null resolve; the API's `upsertFolderIpns` unconditionally increments+overwrites `latestCid`, **wiping the real bin record**. Crucially, the API's `/ipns/resolve` already DB-cache-falls-back and writes the row synchronously on publish — so a 404 means "genuinely not there," and publishing empty on read is *never* safe.

**Fix (client-only, no API change):** stop `loadBin` from ever publishing — on no-record, return an in-memory empty `BinState {entries:[], sequenceNumber:0, ipnsName}`; the first `addToBin` lazily creates the real record. Optional bounded retry to ride out transient nulls.

The open question (is the bin row durably written, or never written?) is exactly what local repro settles. Delegating the full stateful loop — bring up (reuse the running stack), reproduce, confirm via the DB, fix, verify green locally, update unit tests, commit — to one agent with the complete playbook:

- **`client.ts`** — two principled defense-in-depth additions: (1) loadBin won't let a transient empty-fallback overwrite a loaded non-empty `binState`; (2) `deleteToBin` self-heals if `binState` is null (prevents the BinNotLoadedError→hard-delete path that silently loses the item). **Keep.**
- **`useBin.ts` / `useAuth.ts`** — store-level guards mirroring (1) for the two racing loaders. Slightly redundant but harmless. **Keep.**
- **`sdk-core/ipns/index.ts`** — pure `[DIAG-PUB]` debug instrumentation the agent forgot to remove. **Revert.**

> AGENT

**Smoking gun.** The navigation timeline shows the exact bounce:

```
push #/bin       ← test clicks Bin nav (step 6) ✓
push #/          ← BinPage.tsx:29  navigate('/')   ← THE BOUNCE
push #/files     ← Login.tsx:49    navigate('/files')
```

So clicking `/bin` mounts `BinPage`, whose **"redirect if not authenticated" guard fires `navigate('/')`** → Login → `/files`. The bin never renders. This is a **BinPage auth-guard race during post-reload session restore** — not the SDK, not the bin data, not `useFolderNavigation`. The new #498 test is the first to reload→open-bin, so it's the first to hit this latent BinPage bug.

FilesPage and BinPage have **identical** guards (`if (!isLoading && !isAuthenticated) navigate('/')`), and `isAuthenticated` comes straight from the store. FilesPage survives because it mounts *during* `isLoading=true` and by the time loading clears, auth is set. BinPage mounts *later* (on the bin click) and bounces — so the store's `isAuthenticated` is false at that instant despite `user-menu` being visible. > AGENT

`isAuthenticated` is the raw store value, and `isLoading = !coreKitInitialized || isLoggingIn || isLoggingOut`. That exposes a **race gap**: right after `coreKitInitialized` flips true but *before* `restoreSession` sets `isLoggingIn=true`/`isAuthenticated=true`, there's a window where `!isLoading && !isAuthenticated` is briefly true → the protected-route guard redirects to `/`. FilesPage rides it out (mounted during loading); BinPage, mounting fresh on the bin click, lands in the gap and bounces. This affects all four protected routes.

The clean one-line fix: keep `isLoading` true while a CoreKit session is pending restore. Let me confirm `coreKitLoggedIn` is in scope, then apply it.

Keeping isLoading true until restore\n  // resolves closes that gap; a genuinely logged-out user has coreKitLoggedIn\n  // false, so the login redirect still fires.\n  const isLoading =\n    !coreKitInitialized || isLoggingIn || isLoggingOut || (coreKitLoggedIn && !isAuthenticated);"
}

Summary of the real fix (3 parts, all confirmed):
1. **`useAuth.ts isLoading` guard** (my fix) — closes the post-reload restore-window gap so BinPage doesn't bounce `/bin → /login → /files`.
2. **`loadBin` no-clobber + `deleteToBin` self-heal** (agent's, committed `73c9f037a`) — item reaches the bin and isn't wiped by an empty auto-repair.
3. The step-8 429 was a **local-only** `NODE_ENV=development` throttle artifact — gone under CI's `NODE_ENV=test`.

diff --git a/apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts b/apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts
index 24f9d838b..600e22aaa 100644
--- a/apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts
+++ b/apps/web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts
@@ -91,7 +91,16 @@ export function useAuth() {
   const pendingAuthMethod = useAuthStore((s) => s.pendingAuthMethod);
   const setPendingAuth = useAuthStore((s) => s.setPendingAuth);
 
-  const isLoading = !coreKitInitialized || isLoggingIn || isLoggingOut;
+  // `coreKitLoggedIn && !isAuthenticated` covers the session-restore window: after
+  // a reload CoreKit re-initializes (coreKitInitialized flips true) a beat before
+  // the restoreSession effect sets isLoggingIn/isAuthenticated. Without this term
+  // there is a transient where !isLoading && !isAuthenticated are both true, so a
+  // protected route mounting in that gap (e.g. opening /bin right after a reload)
+  // wrongly redirects to /login. Keeping isLoading true until restore resolves
+  // closes the gap; a genuinely logged-out user has coreKitLoggedIn false, so the
+  // login redirect still fires.
+  const isLoading =
+    !coreKitInitialized || isLoggingIn || isLoggingOut || (coreKitLoggedIn && !isAuthenticated);
 
   // Get vault store actions
   const setVaultKeys = useVaultStore((state) => state.setVaultKeys);
