> AGENT

Both root causes are pinned with **high confidence**, and the adversarial synthesis agents *refuted* the two initial hypotheses where they were wrong (the link-invite "no recipient pubkey" theory — refuted; the duplicate-key — confirmed benign pre-existing TOCTOU noise, off the critical path). Two independent, surgical regressions:

**F1 — invite-link 400:** REQ-4 (48-06) made the web send `itemName: ''` (name moved to `itemNameEncrypted`), but `CreateInviteDto.itemName` still has `@MinLength(1)` while the sibling `CreateShareDto` was correctly relaxed → 400. Fix: drop `@MinLength(1)` from `create-invite.dto.ts` + `pnpm api:generate`.

**F2 — "Shared folder not loaded":** REQ-3 (48-04) routed the recipient save through `client.updateSharedFile` (gated by `requireSharedFolder`), but the **standalone-file** open branch in `useSharedNavigationActions.ts` never seeds the SDK `sharedFolderTree` (only folder branches do). Fix: seed in the file branch.

The F2 fix hinges on exactly what `seedActiveSharedFolder` does (if it resolves the IPNS as a *folder* it'd break for a file share). I'll verify the seed mechanism and both DTOs myself before directing the executor — reading the critical files now.

83	export function useSharedNavigationActions(p: SharedNavigationActionsParams) {
84	  /**
85	   * Navigate into a shared folder/file from the top-level list.
86	   */
87	  const navigateToShare = useCallback(
88	    async (shareId: string) => {
89	      const auth = useAuthStore.getState();
90	      if (!auth.vaultKeypair) {
91	        p.setError('No keypair available');
92	        return;
93	      }
94	
95	      const shareItem = p.sharedItems.find((s) => s.share.shareId === shareId);
96	      if (!shareItem) return;
97	
98	      const share = shareItem.share;
99	
100	      p.setIsLoading(true);
101	      p.setError(null);
102	      p.clearPolling();
103	
104	      try {
105	        const itemKey = await unwrapKey(
106	          hexToBytes(share.encryptedKey),
107	          auth.vaultKeypair.privateKey
108	        );
109	
110	        if (share.itemType === 'folder') {
111	          let folderKeyStored = false;
112	          try {
113	            const resolved = await resolveIpnsRecord(share.ipnsName);
114	            if (!resolved) throw new Error('Could not resolve shared folder IPNS');
115	
116	            const encryptedBytes = await fetchFromIpfs(resolved.cid);
117	            const encryptedJson = new TextDecoder().decode(encryptedBytes);
118	            const encrypted: EncryptedFolderMetadata = JSON.parse(encryptedJson);
119	            const metadata = await decryptFolderMetadata(encrypted, itemKey);
120	
121	            if (share.permission === 'write' && share.encryptedIpnsKey) {
122	              try {
123	                const ipnsPrivKey = await unwrapKey(
124	                  hexToBytes(share.encryptedIpnsKey),
125	                  auth.vaultKeypair.privateKey
126	                );
127	                p.ipnsPrivateKeyRef.current = ipnsPrivKey;
128	              } catch (err) {
129	                logger.error('[SharedNav] Failed to unwrap IPNS key for write share:', err);
130	              }
131	            }
132	
133	            const children = metadata.children ?? [];
134	            const seqNum = BigInt(resolved.sequenceNumber);
135	            p.setCurrentView('folder');
136	            p.setCurrentShareId(shareId);
137	            p.setFolderChildren(children);
138	            p.folderChildrenRef.current = children;
139	            p.setFolderKey(itemKey);
140	            folderKeyStored = true;
141	            p.setBreadcrumbs([{ id: shareId, name: share.itemName }]);
142	            p.setPermission(p.ipnsPrivateKeyRef.current ? share.permission : 'read');
143	            p.setIpnsName(share.ipnsName);
144	            p.setCurrentSequenceNumber(seqNum);
145	            p.sequenceNumberRef.current = seqNum;
146	            p.navStackRef.current = [];
147	
148	            // Seed the SDK as the single owner of shared write state for this
149	            // depth (REQ-3). Only write shares (IPNS key present) can mutate.
150	            if (p.ipnsPrivateKeyRef.current && auth.vaultKeypair) {
151	              p.seedActiveSharedFolder({
152	                shareId,
153	                ipnsName: share.ipnsName,
154	                folderKey: itemKey,
155	                ipnsPrivateKey: p.ipnsPrivateKeyRef.current,
156	                sequenceNumber: seqNum,
157	                children,
158	                ownerPublicKey: parsePublicKey(share.sharerPublicKey),
159	                recipientPublicKey: auth.vaultKeypair.publicKey,
160	              });
161	            }
162	          } finally {
163	            if (!folderKeyStored) itemKey.fill(0);
164	          }
165	        } else {
166	          let folderKeyStored = false;
167	          try {
168	            if (share.permission === 'write' && share.encryptedIpnsKey) {
169	              try {
170	                const ipnsPrivKey = await unwrapKey(
171	                  hexToBytes(share.encryptedIpnsKey),
172	                  auth.vaultKeypair.privateKey
173	                );
174	                p.ipnsPrivateKeyRef.current = ipnsPrivKey;
175	              } catch (err) {
176	                logger.error('[SharedNav] Failed to unwrap IPNS key for write file share:', err);
177	              }
178	            }
179	            p.setCurrentView('file');
180	            p.setCurrentShareId(shareId);
181	            p.setFolderKey(itemKey);
182	            folderKeyStored = true;
183	            p.setPermission(p.ipnsPrivateKeyRef.current ? share.permission : 'read');
184	            p.setIpnsName(share.ipnsName);
185	            p.setBreadcrumbs([{ id: shareId, name: share.itemName }]);
186	          } finally {
187	            if (!folderKeyStored) itemKey.fill(0);
188	          }
189	        }
190	      } catch (err) {
191	        logger.error('[SharedNav] Failed to navigate to shared item:', err);
192	        p.setError('Failed to open shared item');
193	      } finally {
194	        p.setIsLoading(false);

206	      if (!auth.vaultKeypair || !p.currentShareId) return;
207	
208	      p.setIsLoading(true);
209	      p.setError(null);
210	      p.clearPolling();

212	      try {

216	
217	        const subfolderKey = await unwrapKey(
218	          hexToBytes(keyRecord.encryptedKey),

220	        );
221	        let subfolderKeyStored = false;
222	
223	        try {
224	          const folderEntry = p.folderChildren.find(

226	          );

228	
229	          const resolved = await resolveIpnsRecord(folderEntry.ipnsName);
230	          if (!resolved) throw new Error('Could not resolve subfolder IPNS');
231	
232	          const encryptedBytes = await fetchFromIpfs(resolved.cid);
233	          const encryptedJson = new TextDecoder().decode(encryptedBytes);
234	          const encrypted: EncryptedFolderMetadata = JSON.parse(encryptedJson);
235	          const metadata = await decryptFolderMetadata(encrypted, subfolderKey);
236	
237	          if (p.folderKey && p.ipnsName) {
238	            p.navStackRef.current.push({
239	              folderId: p.breadcrumbs[p.breadcrumbs.length - 1]?.id ?? '',
240	              folderName: p.breadcrumbs[p.breadcrumbs.length - 1]?.name ?? '',
241	              children: p.folderChildren,
242	              folderKey: p.folderKey,
243	              ipnsName: p.ipnsName,
244	              sequenceNumber: p.currentSequenceNumber,
245	            });
246	          }
247	
248	          const children = metadata.children ?? [];
249	          const seqNum = BigInt(resolved.sequenceNumber);
250	          p.setFolderChildren(children);
251	          p.folderChildrenRef.current = children;
252	          p.setFolderKey(subfolderKey);
253	          subfolderKeyStored = true;
254	          p.setBreadcrumbs((prev) => [...prev, { id: folderId, name: folderName }]);
255	          p.setIpnsName(folderEntry.ipnsName);
256	          p.setCurrentSequenceNumber(seqNum);
257	          p.sequenceNumberRef.current = seqNum;

260	            p.zeroIpnsKey();

308	      }
309	    },

313	      p.folderKey,

315	      p.getShareKeys,
316	      p.ipnsName,
317	      p.currentSequenceNumber,
318	      p.clearPolling,

`seedActiveSharedFolder` takes explicit children/sequence/keys (it's a direct seed, given the folder branch passes resolved values — not a resolver). That makes the file-branch fix viable with `children: []`, `sequenceNumber: 0n`. But I must confirm two things before applying: (1) the seed path doesn't internally *resolve* the IPNS as a folder, and (2) `updateSharedFile` (file path) doesn't consume `state.children`/`sequenceNumber`/folder `ipnsName`. Reading the seed mechanism + SDK write path.

56	/**
57	 * Seed / re-seed the SDK's sharedFolderTree for the active shared folder.
58	 *
59	 * The SDK keys shared state by `shareId`, but the web navigates through
60	 * subfolders within a single share — each with a distinct ipnsName / folderKey /
61	 * ipnsPrivateKey / sequence. So this is invoked on EVERY navigation point that
62	 * changes the active folder context (share-enter, subfolder-enter, up,
63	 * breadcrumb), overwriting the prior depth's state under the same shareId.
64	 *
65	 * `SharedFolderTree.set()` clones the key buffers, so the caller's `folderKey` /
66	 * `ipnsPrivateKey` buffers are never zeroed by the SDK.
67	 */
68	export function seedSharedFolder(client: SharedFolderClient, args: SeedSharedFolderArgs): void {
69	  const state: SharedFolderState = {
70	    shareId: args.shareId,
71	    ipnsName: args.ipnsName,
72	    folderKey: args.folderKey,
73	    ipnsPrivateKey: args.ipnsPrivateKey,
74	    sequenceNumber: args.sequenceNumber,
75	    children: args.children,
76	    ownerPublicKey: args.ownerPublicKey,
77	    recipientPublicKey: args.recipientPublicKey,
78	    addShareKeysFn: args.addShareKeysFn,
79	  };
80	  client.loadSharedFolder(args.shareId, state);
81	}
82	
83	/** Callback shape for the projection: receives the SDK's authoritative state. */
84	export type SharedFolderProjectionApply = (children: FolderChild[], sequenceNumber: bigint) => void;
85	
86	/**
87	 * Subscribe to `sharedFolder:updated` and project the SDK's authoritative
88	 * children + sequence into the web refs/state — the ONLY writer of those refs
89	 * post-mutation (T-48-09). Events for a different shareId than the active one
90	 * are ignored (T-48-10: no cross-share state bleed at the projection layer).
91	 *
92	 * `getActiveShareId` is read at event time (not closed over) so the same
93	 * subscription stays correct as the active share changes.
94	 *
95	 * Note: `updateSharedFile` emits with UNCHANGED children/sequence (file-only
96	 * metadata publish) — the projection applies it as a no-op-on-data re-resolve
97	 * signal, which is safe because children/sequence are identical.
98	 *
99	 * @returns the unsubscribe function (call on unmount / share-change).
100	 */
101	export function subscribeSharedFolderProjection(
102	  client: SharedFolderClient,
103	  getActiveShareId: () => string | null,
104	  apply: SharedFolderProjectionApply
105	): () => void {
106	  return client.on((event) => {
107	    if (event.type !== 'sharedFolder:updated') return;
108	    if (event.shareId !== getActiveShareId()) return;
109	    apply(event.children, event.sequenceNumber);
110	  });
111	}

`seedSharedFolder` calls `client.loadSharedFolder(shareId, state)` with a **fully-built state object** — it's a direct seed, no IPNS resolution. So seeding the file branch with `children: []` / `sequenceNumber: 0n` is safe (no folder-resolve on a file IPNS). Final check: confirm `updateSharedFile` + `buildSharedWriteContextFromState` don't depend on `state.children`/`sequenceNumber`.

So if I revert the ordering churn, `openapi.json` is clean and the hook passes. Since my DTO change produces **zero** semantic spec change (no `minLength` emitted, client source unchanged), reverting the 714-line noise is correct and keeps the PR clean.

## REUSE review — Phase 48 diff

The diff is largely well-factored: it correctly reuses the existing CAS engine (`publishWithCas`), `loadFolderMetadata`, `withRevocationGuard`, `ShareKeyCache`, `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey`, and mirrors the owned-path `FolderTree`/projection patterns rather than forking them. A few genuine duplications:

### Findings

**1. `parsePublicKey` re-implements the 0x-strip that `hexToBytes` already does**
- file: `apps/web/src/hooks/shared-folder-projection.ts`
- line: 21-25
- summary: `parsePublicKey(keyHex)` strips an optional `0x` prefix then calls `hexToBytes`, but `hexToBytes` already strips `0x` internally.
- cost: Redundant wrapper. `hexToBytes` (`packages/crypto/src/utils/encoding.ts:14-15`: `const cleanHex = hex.startsWith('0x') ? hex.slice(2) : hex;`) already handles the prefix. The 4 call sites in `useSharedNavigationActions.ts` (lines 158, 201, 313, 390) can call `hexToBytes(share.sharerPublicKey)` directly (it's already imported there at line 17). Delete `parsePublicKey` and its test.
- confidence: high

**2. Manual `startsWith('0x') ? .slice(2) : x` before `hexToBytes` for recipient pubkeys — same redundancy, in changed share/invite code**
- file: `apps/web/src/services/share.service.ts`
- line: 194-198 (also pre-existing at 482-486, 616-620)
- summary: New `backfillSentShareItemNames` hand-strips the `0x` prefix from `recipientPublicKey` before `hexToBytes`.

I reviewed the 9 focus files against current contents. ### Findings

**1. `ensureFolderLoaded` resolves each subfolder's IPNS sequentially during DFS**
- file: `packages/sdk/src/client.ts`, lines 469–510
- cost: The self-bootstrap walk pops one folder at a time and `await`s `loadFolder` (IPNS resolve + IPFS fetch + decrypt) for each child *serially* inside the `for` loop. For a deep/wide tree, reaching a target N levels down with M siblings per level does M×N sequential network round-trips on the *first* navigation/op after reload. Cheaper: resolve a level's unloaded children concurrently with `Promise.all` (bounded by `pLimit`, which is already a dep) before descending — same early-exit semantics, but per-level latency instead of per-folder. This is on a cold hot-path (first mutation after reload), so it's user-visible.
- confidence: medium (correctness-preserving but a non-trivial refactor; flagging the cost, not mandating the change)

**2. `loadBin` retry loop is 6 attempts × 500ms fixed = up to ~2.5s of blocking I/O on a genuinely-empty bin**
- file: `packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts`, lines 172–230 (constants 173–175, loop 202–219)
- cost: A brand-new user (no bin record ever published) pays all 6 `resolveIpnsRecord` calls plus 5×500ms sleeps (~2.5s) every `loadBin` before falling back to empty state. `loadBin` is fire-and-forget on login *and* called on BinBrowser mount, so two such 2.5s walks can run per session for users who've never deleted anything. The retry exists to recover transient cold-cache nulls, but a genuinely-absent record can't be distinguished from a transient one, so the common new-user case always pays worst-case. Cheaper: exponential backoff (matching `publishWithVerify`'s `500·2^attempt`) reaches similar total coverage in fewer attempts, or cap at 3 attempts — the cold-cache window after a reload is short. Confirm against product expectation for first-login latency.
- confidence: medium

**3. `getShareKeys` cache (60s TTL) is bypassed by `updateSharedFileHandler`, which calls `fetchShareKeys` directly**
- file: `apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedWriteOps.ts`, line 140 (`const keys = await fetchShareKeys(shareId)`)
- cost: Every shared-file content update re-fetches all share keys from the API even though `useSharedNavigation` maintains a `ShareKeyCache` (`shareKeysCacheRef`, 60s TTL) that the navigation actions use via `getShareKeys`. The write hook isn't given the cache ref, so it always hits the network. Note: this exact call pre-exists on `origin/main` (verified) — the Phase-48 diff did not introduce it — so it's out of scope for "wasted work the diff introduces." Flagging only because it's adjacent and the cheaper path (thread `getShareKeys` into the write hook) already exists.

**4. `subscribeSharedFolderProjection` closure is correctly scoped — no leak**
- file: `apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedNavigation.ts`, lines 270–283; `shared-folder-projection.ts` 101–111
- cost: none. The subscription effect has `[]` deps and reads the active shareId via `currentShareIdRef` (a ref updated each render at line 137) rather than closing over `currentShareId`. This is the *right* pattern — it avoids resubscribing on every share change and doesn't capture stale large scopes. The unsubscribe is returned and the SDK emitter holds only the small handler. No long-lived large-scope capture. Confirmed not a memory concern.
- confidence: high (this is a non-finding / already efficient)

Cheaper would be a single-share status endpoint; absent that, it's a known cost. Flagging for completeness per the "30s poller path" angle.

The genuinely diff-introduced efficiency items are **#1** (serial DFS bootstrap) and **#2** (fixed 6×500ms bin retry) — both bounded, both on cold paths, neither a correctness risk. #3 and #5 are real waste but pre-date this branch. The new projection/refresh consolidation (subscription + `refreshSharedFolder`) is well-designed: stable subscription, ref-based shareId read, single ref-writer, and the #489 sequence guard avoids redundant re-emits clobbering fresh state. No long-lived large-scope closures or memory leaks introduced. Key-zeroing invariants are untouched.

**1. Per-depth re-seed dance signals the SDK shared-tree is keyed one level too shallow**
- **file**: `packages/sdk/src/state/shared-folder-tree.ts` (keyed by `shareId`); driven from `apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedNavigationActions.ts:151,194,306,383` (4 seed/re-seed sites)

The root cause: `SharedFolderTree` is keyed by `shareId` only, but a single share is browsed across multiple subfolder depths, each with a distinct `ipnsName`/`folderKey`/`ipnsPrivateKey`/`sequence`. So each nav step *overwrites* the same `shareId` slot, and the web must re-supply the full resolved context every time.
- **cost**: This is the parallel-state pattern the owned path already dissolved. The owned `folderTree` is keyed by `ipnsName` and self-bootstraps via `ensureFolderLoaded` (DFS from root, unwrapping each child's `folderKeyEncrypted`/`ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted`). The shared path has *no equivalent self-load*: there's no `ensureSharedFolderLoaded` that, given a `shareId` + target subfolder `ipnsName`, walks from the share root resolving subfolder keys via the share-keys API. The deeper form keys shared depths by `ipnsName` (under a share context) or adds a shared DFS-loader so the web seeds once at share entry and the SDK resolves descendants. The web carries ~120 lines of resolution/re-seed logic (`reseedRestoredDepth`, `restoreIpnsKeyForDepth`, the inline subfolder-key unwrap in `navigateToSubfolder`) that is exactly the "parallel shared-folder logic that should live in the SDK."
- **worth_doing_now**: **no** — this is a real altitude gap but a large, risky refactor (new SDK loader contract, share-key fetch plumbing into the SDK, depth-keyed tree). 48-07 only added `refreshSharedFolder` (single-depth re-resolve), which is a deliberate incremental step. Do it as a dedicated follow-up phase, not inside this PR. Note it explicitly so the "SDK owns shared state" goal isn't considered fully met.
- **confidence**: high

---

**2. Standalone-file-share seed is an acceptable parallel branch, not a deep bandaid**
- **file**: `apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedNavigationActions.ts:193-204` (commit `288d0670a`)
- **summary**: The recent fix adds a second `seedActiveSharedFolder` call in the file-share branch (`children: []`, `sequenceNumber: 0n`) so `updateSharedFile → requireSharedFolder` has state.
- **cost**: It *looks* like a special-case bandaid, but unlike the owned path it is **not** self-bootstrappable: a standalone file share has no parent folder reachable from a root the recipient holds keys for — the recipient only ever holds the file's own key + IPNS key. There is no root to DFS from (the owned `ensureFolderLoaded` self-heal depends on `rootIpnsKeypair`, which a share recipient does not have). So "seed at entry" is the correct altitude here; the file and folder branches both seed because both are entry points and neither can lazy-load. The duplication between the two branches (folder vs file seed blocks) is the only smell, and it's minor.
- **worth_doing_now**: **no** (the fix itself is correct). Optional tiny cleanup: both `navigateToShare` branches build a near-identical seed args object — could be hoisted to one helper. Low value; skip unless touching the file anyway.
- **confidence**: high

**3. REQ-4 itemName encryption is symmetric across create-share / create-invite / claim — well-leveled**
- **file**: `apps/web/src/services/share.service.ts:251-256`, `apps/web/src/services/invite.service.ts:188-198, 261-269`, `apps/web/src/components/file-browser/ShareDialog.tsx:332-336`
- **summary**: All three create paths consistently send `itemName: '' + itemNameEncrypted` (ciphertext-only). The split is centralized in `createShare` (`itemName: params.itemNameEncrypted ? '' : params.itemName`); `createInviteLink` and `claimInvite` follow the same wrap/re-wrap shape. API DTOs uniformly relaxed `@MinLength(1)` (the `be022ffcb` fix aligned create-invite to create-share) and added the same `itemNameEncrypted` bytea column + hex projection across all entities/controllers. No asymmetric special-casing.

'' : ...` branch — so the "wrap the name" logic lives in *two* places (the dialog computes ciphertext, `createShare` decides plaintext-vs-empty). Folding the wrap into `createShare` (take `recipientPublicKey` + plaintext name, wrap internally) would make `createShare` the single owner of the REQ-4 contract and remove the chance a future caller forgets to wrap.
- **worth_doing_now**: **no** — the dialog already passes a `recipientPubKeyBytes` it computed for the key wrap, so inlining is convenient but not load-bearing; current form is consistent and tested. Note as a small follow-up.
- **confidence**: medium

---

**4. `backfillSentShareItemNames` is a no-op stub blocked on a missing API endpoint — wrong altitude to ship**

- **summary**: The lazy-backfill function computes the re-wrapped ciphertext, then `void itemNameEncrypted` + `logger.debug('...pending API update endpoint')` and returns a count — there is no persist because no `PATCH /shares/:id { itemNameEncrypted }` endpoint exists. It runs on every owner share-list load.
- **cost**: This is dead computation at the wrong altitude: it does ECIES wrap work + a debug log per legacy row on every `fetchAllSentShares`, persists nothing, and the `backfilled` count is meaningless (counts "eligible," not "done"). The honest forms are either (a) don't ship the backfill until the API endpoint lands (the predicate `shouldBackfill` + `decryptItemName` are the only parts with present value), or (b) land the one-line API endpoint this phase so the backfill actually does something. Shipping a self-described-blocked stub that burns crypto cycles on every list load is the bandaid.
- **worth_doing_now**: **yes (lightweight)** — gate the fire-and-forget call (`:390-392`) behind the endpoint's existence, or strip the per-row wrap+log loop down to a count-only `shouldBackfill` tally (no wasted `wrapKey`), until the PATCH endpoint exists. Keep `decryptItemName`/`shouldBackfill` (they're used by the read path). The SUMMARY already flags T-48-18 as "accept," so leaving it is defensible — but the wasted per-row `wrapKey` on every load is cheap to remove now.
- **confidence**: medium

---

**5. `updateSharedFile` file-only emit re-purposes `sharedFolder:updated` as a "re-resolve" signal — acceptable, document the overload**
- **file**: `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:2152-2160`; consumed at `apps/web/src/hooks/shared-folder-projection.ts:106-110`
- **summary**: `updateSharedFile` emits `sharedFolder:updated` with *unchanged* children/sequence purely to nudge the projection to re-resolve the file. The projection applies it as a no-op-on-data.

Fine as-is; the comments already explain it.
- **worth_doing_now**: **no**.
- **confidence**: high

---

### Summary
The REQ-4 itemName work (findings 3) is well-leveled and symmetric. The standalone-file seed (finding 2) is correctly at the right depth, not a bandaid — it can't self-bootstrap by design. The one structural altitude gap worth flagging loudly is **finding 1**: the web still owns ~120 lines of per-depth shared-folder resolution/re-seed because `SharedFolderTree` is keyed by `shareId` instead of by depth (`ipnsName`), and there's no shared analog of `ensureFolderLoaded`. That's the unfinished half of "SDK owns shared-folder state" — defer to a follow-up phase, don't expand this PR. The one cheap fix worth doing now is **finding 4**: stop the blocked `backfillSentShareItemNames` from burning a `wrapKey` per legacy row on every share-list load while it persists nothing.

---

## Security Review: Phase 48 REQ-3 (SDK-owned shared-folder write state)

### Invariant verdicts

KEY-ZEROING INVARIANT: HOLDS (with one LOW-severity residue caveat consistent with the pre-existing owned-path convention).
CROSS-SHARE ISOLATION INVARIANT: HOLDS.

I traced every unwrapped `folderKey` / `ipnsPrivateKey` through seed -> SDK clone -> write -> teardown, confirmed `set()` clones (no caller-buffer aliasing), `delete()`/`clear()` zero, stateless ops zero only ephemeral keys they generate, and no key material reaches logs or the server in plaintext.

---

### Findings

**[LOW] `SharedFolderTree.set()` orphans the previous entry's key buffers without zeroing on re-seed / adopt**
- `packages/sdk/src/state/shared-folder-tree.ts:34-40`
- Description: When `set()` overwrites an existing `shareId`, the prior entry's cloned `folderKey`/`ipnsPrivateKey` buffers are dropped to GC without `.fill(0)`. This path is hit on every navigation re-seed (`loadSharedFolder`) and every `adoptSharedFolderResult` (`client.ts:2039`) — i.e. after each upload/rename/delete/refresh, since `adoptSharedFolderResult` spreads the existing tree state and calls `set()` again, re-cloning the keys and orphaning the previous clones.
- Impact: Decrypted AES folder key + Ed25519 IPNS private key residue lingers in heap memory until GC. Exploitation requires local memory disclosure (heap dump / Spectre-class). Low practical risk; same exposure window as any GC'd `Uint8Array`.
- Note on calibration: The owned-path `FolderTree.set()` (`packages/sdk/src/state/folder-tree.ts:29-38`) uses the identical clone-on-set-no-zero-on-overwrite pattern, so this is a consistent, pre-existing codebase convention rather than a REQ-3 regression. The class doc comment ("set() clones key buffers so caller buffers are never zeroed") is accurate but does not claim to zero the previous internal clone.
- Recommendation (optional, defense-in-depth): In `set()`, read the existing entry first and zero its `folderKey`/`ipnsPrivateKey` before overwriting:
  ```ts
  set(shareId: string, state: SharedFolderState): void {
    const prev = this.shares.get(shareId);
    if (prev) {
      prev.folderKey?.fill(0);
      prev.ipnsPrivateKey?.fill(0);
    }
    this.shares.set(shareId, { ...state, folderKey: new Uint8Array(state.folderKey), ipnsPrivateKey: new Uint8Array(state.ipnsPrivateKey) });
  }
  ```
  Caveat: `adoptSharedFolderResult` (`client.ts:2030-2039`) spreads `state` (the live tree entry) and re-passes its `folderKey`/`ipnsPrivateKey` into `set()`. If `set()` zeroed-before-clone naively, it would zero the source buffer before cloning it. The fix above is safe because it clones from `state` (the caller's object, which after spread still references the same buffers as `prev`) — so for the adopt path you must zero `prev` only when `prev.folderKey !== state.folderKey`. Given that subtlety and the matching owned-path convention, leaving this as-is is defensible; flagging for awareness only.

**[LOW] `getAll()` / `getSharedFolderState()` expose live internal key buffers by reference**
- `packages/sdk/src/state/shared-folder-tree.ts:70-72` and `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:1984-1986`
- Description: `getAll()` returns `new Map(this.shares)` — a shallow Map copy whose values still reference the internal `SharedFolderState` objects, including the live `folderKey`/`ipnsPrivateKey` buffers. `getSharedFolderState()` returns the internal reference directly (the doc comment acknowledges "consumers must not mutate it"). A caller that zeroes a returned key would corrupt SDK state (use-after-zero), or could read it out of band.
- Impact: No current caller in the changed web code abuses this (the web never calls `getSharedFolderState`/`getAll` for shared state; it relies on the projection event). Contrast with the deliberately-copied `getFolderIpnsPrivateKey` (`client.ts:290-294`, returns `new Uint8Array(key)`). Latent footgun, not an active leak.
- Recommendation: Document the reference-sharing contract (already partially done) or return deep copies if any external consumer is added. No action required for REQ-3 as shipped.

**[INFORMATIONAL] IPNS private key handling is correct end-to-end**
- `useSharedNavigationActions.ts:121-131, 168-178, 411-434`; `useSharedNavigation.ts:143-148, 159`; `shared-write.ts:447-507`
- `encryptedIpnsKey` is unwrapped client-side only for `permission === 'write'`, stored in `ipnsPrivateKeyRef` (a ref, never React state, never serialized), zeroed by `zeroIpnsKey()` on `navigateToRoot`, `navigateToSubfolder` depth-change (line 279), `restoreIpnsKeyForDepth` (line 407), `handleRevocation` (line 159), and the load-effect cleanup (line 255). In `shared-write.ts:updateSharedFile`, the file-level `ipnsPrivKey` from `getFileIpnsKeyFn` is zeroed in a `finally` (line 503). The unwrapped key is never passed to the server (only `updateSharePermission` forwards the already-ECIES-`encryptedIpnsKey` string, `shared-write.ts:519-532`). HOLDS.

**[INFORMATIONAL] New standalone-file-share seed block (file branch) is correct**
- `useSharedNavigationActions.ts:165-208`
- The `folderKeyStored = true` flag (line 182) correctly suppresses the `finally` zeroing of `itemKey` (line 206), because `itemKey` is retained in web state via `setFolderKey(itemKey)` (line 181) and the SDK seed clones it (`SharedFolderTree.set`). No double-free: web owns its `itemKey` copy (zeroed later via `navigateToRoot`/cleanup), SDK owns its clone (zeroed via `delete`/`clear`). The seed only fires when `ipnsPrivateKeyRef.current` is set (write share, line 193), so read-only file shares never seed mutable state. The `sequenceNumber: 0n` / `children: []` placeholders are inert because `updateSharedFile` is file-only and ignores them. No leak, no use-after-zero. HOLDS.

**[INFORMATIONAL] Cross-share isolation holds at every layer**
- Keying by `shareId` (`shared-folder-tree.ts:26`), per-share owner/recipient pubkeys + `addShareKeysFn` carried through `buildSharedWriteContextFromState` (`client.ts:2008-2023`), and the projection's `event.shareId !== getActiveShareId()` filter (`shared-folder-projection.ts:108`) all enforce isolation. `buildSharedWriteContext` (`context.ts:40-53`) passes per-share keys by reference with no shared mutable defaults. No path observed where one share's `folderKey`/IPNS key flows into another share's write context. HOLDS.

**[INFORMATIONAL] No key material in logs or errors**
- All `logger.error`/`console.warn` sites in the changed files (`useSharedNavigationActions.ts:129,176,210,323,547,563`; `shared-write.ts:224,325,485,500`; `useSharedWriteOps.ts:66`; `useSharedNavigation.ts:235`) log only `Error` objects / static strings, never key bytes. The `unwrapKey`-failure logs (lines 129/176) log the thrown error, not the ciphertext or key. HOLDS.

---

### False-positive uncertainty

- The LOW residue finding is calibrated down deliberately: it is the established codebase pattern (owned `FolderTree.set` is identical), so it may be an accepted design tradeoff rather than a defect. I could not exercise the GC behavior statically.
- I did not run tests (per constraint), so I cannot confirm the `adoptSharedFolderResult` -> `set()` re-clone behaves identically under the test harness; my read of the spread semantics (`client.ts:2034-2039`) is static-analysis-based.
- I reviewed only the seven named files plus their direct type/helper dependencies (`types.ts`, `context.ts`, `error.ts`, `folder-tree.ts`). I did not audit `addShareKeys` / `fetchShareKeys` service internals or the API server, which are outside REQ-3 scope.

---

### Overall risk level for REQ-3 key handling: LOW

The two core invariants (key-zeroing on all failure/teardown/revocation paths, and cross-share isolation) HOLD. No CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings. The only issues are two LOW-severity, latent, defense-in-depth memory-residue items that match pre-existing owned-path conventions and require local memory disclosure to exploit. No plaintext key reaches the server or logs; no buffer aliasing between web and SDK; no double-free or use-after-zero in the new standalone-file-share seed path.

Relevant files:

I have all the evidence needed. The `itemName` ECIES wrap uses the exact same `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` primitive (eciesjs: ephemeral key per call + ECDH + HKDF + AES-GCM) as `encryptedKey`. Fresh ephemeral key per call means no IV/nonce reuse. Here are my findings.

---

## Security Review: Phase 48 REQ-4 (encrypt share `itemName` at rest)

### Zero-knowledge invariant: HOLDS (for new code paths)

The server receives only client-produced ECIES ciphertext, stores it verbatim as `bytea`, and never encrypts, decrypts, or derives `itemName`. Confirmed at:
- `apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts:100` — `itemNameEncrypted: dto.itemNameEncrypted ? Buffer.from(dto.itemNameEncrypted, 'hex') : null` (hex→Buffer only)
- `apps/api/src/shares/share-invite.service.ts:47` and `:200` — same verbatim store on create and claim
- Controllers (`shares.controller.ts:75,109,146`, `invites.controller.ts:112`, `share-invites.controller.ts:72,124`) only do `Buffer.toString('hex')` on read
- Migration `1749200000000-EncryptShareItemName.ts` is additive nullable `bytea` with no data `UPDATE` (server cannot encrypt legacy plaintext — correct)
- No server-side logging of `itemName`/`itemNameEncrypted` (grep for log+itemName in `apps/api/src/shares/` returned nothing)
- Public unauthenticated invite-status endpoint (`invites.controller.ts:getInviteStatus`) returns only `{ status: 'active' }` — no name leaks pre-auth
- Invite URL fragment carries only the ephemeral private key (`buildInviteUrl`, `invite.service.ts:82-85`); the plaintext name is never placed in the URL

Cryptographic correctness confirmed: `itemName` is wrapped with the identical primitive as `encryptedKey` (`wrapKey`/`unwrapKey`, `ecies/encrypt.ts` + `decrypt.ts`), backed by `eciesjs` (ephemeral keypair per call → ECDH → HKDF → AES-256-GCM authenticated). Fresh ephemeral key per call ⇒ no IV/nonce reuse. All binary handled as `Uint8Array`; transient unwrapped bytes are zeroed (`decryptItemName` finally `unwrapped.fill(0)`; `claimInvite` `plainName.fill(0)`).

---

### Additional confirmations (no finding)

- ShareDialog direct-share path (`ShareDialog.tsx:335-346`) wraps `item.name` with `recipientPubKeyBytes` (the recipient's real key) and sends `itemName: ''` — correct recipient, ciphertext-only.
- Invite create (`invite.service.ts:189-201`) wraps with the ephemeral public key (matching `encryptedKey`), sends `itemName: ''`. Claim (`invite.service.ts:262-269`) unwraps with the ephemeral private key and re-wraps with `vaultKeypair.publicKey` (the recipient's real key) — correct recipient on the resulting Share row; `plainName.fill(0)` zeroes the transient.
- ECIES tests added (`ecies.test.ts:58-72`) prove the primitive round-trips ASCII + multibyte UTF-8 display names; tamper/truncate/wrong-key tests already assert authenticated failure with a generic, oracle-safe error.
- Error paths in `ShareDialog.tsx:378` and `InvitePage.tsx` catch blocks do not log the plaintext name (ShareDialog logs `err`; InvitePage inspects only `err.status`).

### False-positive uncertainty

- I did not run the test suite (per instruction) and did not inspect the compiled `eciesjs` source in `node_modules` (module path lookup failed); the AES-GCM/ephemeral-per-call behavior is asserted from the library's documented contract and the existing passing `ecies.test.ts` (ephemeral-randomness + tamper tests). High confidence, not executed.
- The MEDIUM `Promise.all` finding assumes `unwrapKey` rejects (which the tests confirm it does on bad input) and that `fetchReceivedShares` has no surrounding per-row guard (confirmed by reading lines 115-131). I am confident in the behavior; severity is calibrated as MEDIUM because it is availability-only, not a confidentiality break.
- I traced the live read path to `share.service.fetchReceivedShares` via `useSharedNavigation.ts`. The SDK (`packages/sdk/src/share/index.ts`) has no parallel received-share fetch that maps `itemName`, so I do not believe there is an un-decrypted display path; if a future SDK-based list view is added it must also call `decryptItemName`.

### Overall risk level for REQ-4: LOW

The zero-knowledge invariant HOLDS for the server on all new code paths — the server only ever stores and echoes client ciphertext for `itemName` and never sees plaintext on create/invite/claim. Cryptography is correct (same audited ECIES primitive, authenticated AES-GCM, fresh ephemeral key, keys zeroed). The two things keeping this from "no findings" are: (1) the MEDIUM availability bug where one bad ciphertext row blocks the whole received-shares list — worth fixing before ship — and (2) the backfill being a structural no-op, meaning legacy/pre-deploy share and invite display names remain plaintext at rest on the untrusted server until a future PATCH endpoint lands (documented transitional state, but it means at-rest encryption is forward-only, not retroactive).

In @apps/api/src/shares/dto/claim-invite.dto.ts around lines 52 - 64, The @MaxLength validator on the itemNameEncrypted field is set to 1024 characters, which is insufficient to handle worst-case UTF-8 encoding of 255-character display names plus ECIES encryption overhead. Increase the @MaxLength value from 1024 to 2500 on the itemNameEncrypted property in the ClaimInviteDto class to safely accommodate the encrypted hex-encoded ciphertext.

### [CRITICAL] apps/api/src/shares/dto/create-invite.dto.ts
In @apps/api/src/shares/dto/create-invite.dto.ts around lines 66 - 78, The @MaxLength(1024) constraint on the itemNameEncrypted field is insufficient to handle worst-case UTF-8 encoding. A 255-character itemName with maximum UTF-8 byte expansion (1020 bytes plaintext) plus ECIES encryption overhead (~97 bytes) requires approximately 2234 hex characters. Increase the @MaxLength value on the itemNameEncrypted property to at least 2234 (or a reasonable upper bound that accommodates this worst-case scenario plus margin for safety).

### [CRITICAL] apps/api/src/shares/dto/create-share.dto.ts
In @apps/api/src/shares/dto/create-share.dto.ts around lines 80 - 92, The @MaxLength(1024) constraint on the itemNameEncrypted field in CreateShareDto is insufficient to accommodate worst-case UTF-8 item names with ECIES encryption overhead. Since itemName supports up to 255 characters which can be 1020 bytes in UTF-8 worst-case, plus ~97 bytes of ECIES overhead, the ciphertext requires approximately 2234+ hex characters. Increase the @MaxLength value on itemNameEncrypted to at least 2500 to safely handle the 1020-byte UTF-8 plaintext plus ECIES overhead for multi-byte Unicode characters like emoji and CJK characters.

  "content": "## Summary\n\nPhase 48 consolidates shared-folder state ownership in the SDK and hardens share metadata, bundling three pending todos plus the root-cause fix for the `#498` web-e2e regression that surfaced on `main`.\n\n- **REQ-1 — fix the `#498` regression (P0):** the merged `#498` left web-e2e red. Root-caused via the Playwright trace to two layered issues and fixed both:\n  - `loadFolder` now applies a sequence-as-clock guard so a stale IPNS resolve cannot clobber fresher in-memory `folderTree` state.\n  - `loadBin` no longer destructively republishes an empty bin to \"repair\" a transient IPNS 404 (bounded retry; returns in-memory empty state without publishing) — this was the actual bin-restore-after-reload break.\n  - Plus a protected-route `isLoading` fix so `/bin` no longer bounces to `/login` during session restore.\n- **REQ-2 — remove redundant web folder-seeding:** now that the SDK self-bootstraps `folderTree` from the root IPNS key (`#498`), the web no longer calls `ensureFolderRegistered` (14 call sites removed). The SDK's `requireFolder`/`ensureFolderLoaded` chokepoint is the single load path.\n- **REQ-3 — route shared-folder writes through the SDK:** the SDK client now owns shared-folder state (`sharedFolderTree`, keyed by `shareId`) and publishing. Web write hooks read nothing back; a `sharedFolder:updated` event-fed projection is the sole writer of the web refs on both the write and the 30s-poll paths (`refreshSharedFolder`).\n- **REQ-4 — encrypt share `itemName` at rest (Phase-14 finding M1):** the display name is ECIES-wrapped (mirroring `encryptedKey`) and sent as ciphertext; the plaintext field goes as `''`. Additive nullable `item_name_encrypted` column; server stores ciphertext verbatim and never encrypts/decrypts it (zero-knowledge preserved).\n\n## Regressions found and fixed during review\n\nThe first full-phase web-e2e run was red on two share specs; both were root-caused (adversarially, against source) and fixed:\n\n- `invite-link-workflow` 400 — `CreateInviteDto.itemName` still had `@MinLength(1)` while the web now sends `itemName: ''` (the sibling `CreateShareDto` was already relaxed). Dropped the constraint.\n- `writable-shares` \"Shared folder not loaded\" — the standalone **file**-share open branch never seeded the SDK `sharedFolderTree` (only folder branches did), so a recipient's save through `client.updateSharedFile` threw. Seed the file branch.\n\n## Review pipeline\n\n- **`/simplify`** — removed a dead `folderKey` prop, a redundant `0x`-strip, and a stale doc reference.\n- **`/gsd:validate-phase`** — phase is **Nyquist-compliant**; one coverage gap (invite/claim `itemNameEncrypted` persistence) was filled with unit tests.\n- **CodeRabbit** — widened `itemNameEncrypted` `@MaxLength` 1024→2500 (a 255-char multibyte name's ciphertext can exceed 1024 hex chars → 400, same class as the invite regression); added `unloadSharedFolder` on unmount to zero SDK-held key material; removed a stray local secrets backup file.\n- **`/security:review`** — overall risk **LOW**. Zero-knowledge invariant holds (server never sees plaintext `itemName` or unencrypted keys), crypto correct (same ECIES primitive, fresh ephemeral key, authenticated AES-256-GCM), key-zeroing + cross-share isolation hold. One MEDIUM availability finding fixed (one bad ciphertext row no longer denies the whole received-shares list). Report at `.planning/security/REVIEW-2026-06-16-phase48.md`.\n\n## Testing\n\n- Unit suites green across sdk / sdk-core / crypto / web (vitest) and api (jest); new tests for the sequence-guard, bin durability, `sharedFolderTree` isolation, shared-write + `refreshSharedFolder`, the web projection/poll path, ECIES itemName round-trip, and API ciphertext persistence.\n- **web-e2e dispatched against the branch and green** (the REQ-1 acceptance gate + full REQ-2/3/4 coverage).\n- `pnpm typecheck` green.\n\n## Deferred follow-ups (out of scope, tracked)\n\n- `PATCH /shares/:id { itemNameEncrypted }` endpoint to make legacy-row backfill actually persist (REQ-4 at-rest encryption is currently forward-only). Captured todo.\n- `SharedFolderTree` is keyed by `shareId`, so the web re-seeds per nav depth — a deeper \"SDK owns shared refresh\" follow-up would add a shared `ensureFolderLoaded` analog. Plan `48-07` took the first incremental step (`refreshSharedFolder`).\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n"

88	async function saveBinMetadata(params: {

115	  // Publish IPNS record with verification

118	    ipnsPrivateKey: binIpns.privateKey,
119	    cid,

127	/**
128	 * Publish an IPNS record and verify it is resolvable.
129	 *
130	 * Wraps createAndPublishIpnsRecord with a resolve-back verification loop.
131	 * On verify failure, retries with exponential backoff (500ms, 1000ms, 2000ms).
132	 * After all retries exhausted, does NOT throw -- the publish went through,
133	 * verification just couldn't confirm propagation.
134	 */
135	async function publishWithVerify(params: {
136	  ipnsName: string;
137	  ipnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array;
138	  cid: string;
139	  sequenceNumber: bigint;
140	  encryptedIpnsPrivateKey?: string;
141	  keyEpoch?: number;
142	  ctx: SdkContext;
143	  maxRetries?: number;
144	}): Promise<void> {
145	  const maxRetries = params.maxRetries ?? 3;
146	  // Publish once -- the API call is idempotent but no need to repeat it
147	  await sdkCore.createAndPublishIpnsRecord({
148	    ipnsPrivateKey: params.ipnsPrivateKey,
149	    ipnsName: params.ipnsName,
150	    metadataCid: params.cid,
151	    sequenceNumber: params.sequenceNumber,
152	    encryptedIpnsPrivateKey: params.encryptedIpnsPrivateKey,
153	    keyEpoch: params.keyEpoch,
154	    ctx: params.ctx,
155	  });
156	  // Verify with retries: resolve back to confirm DB cache was written
157	  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++) {
158	    const resolved = await sdkCore.resolveIpnsRecord(params.ipnsName, params.ctx);
159	    if (resolved) return;
160	    if (attempt < maxRetries - 1) {
161	      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500 * Math.pow(2, attempt)));
162	    }
163	  }
164	  // After all retries, don't throw -- the publish went through, just verification failed.
165	  // The record may still propagate eventually.
166	}

172	/** Number of resolve attempts in loadBin before falling back to empty state. */
173	const LOAD_BIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 6;
174	/** Base backoff (ms) between loadBin resolve retries. */
175	const LOAD_BIN_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 500;
176	
177	/**
178	 * Load the recycle bin metadata from IPNS.
179	 *
180	 * If no bin IPNS record exists yet (first login / never deleted anything),
181	 * returns an in-memory empty BinState so that deleteToBin can create the first
182	 * record. The first addToBin lazily publishes the real record at
183	 * sequenceNumber 1 (0 + 1), which matches the API create-path.
184	 *
185	 * Crucially, loadBin NEVER publishes on a null resolve. A null is not a
186	 * reliable "bin is empty" signal: resolveIpnsRecord also returns null on a
187	 * cold-cache miss right after a page reload, or while a concurrent
188	 * loadBin()/delete is mid-flight. Publishing an empty record here is
189	 * destructive — the bin publish path carries no expectedSequenceNumber, so the
190	 * API blindly increments the sequence and overwrites the real record's CID with
191	 * the empty-bin CID (apps/api ipns.service upsertFolderIpns), wiping every
192	 * entry. The API's /ipns/resolve already falls back to its synchronously-written
193	 * DB cache, so a client-side null means the record is genuinely absent at that
194	 * instant; we recover transient nulls with a bounded retry instead of writing.
195	 *
196	 * @returns Current bin state (never null — in-memory empty state if no record exists)
197	 */
198	export async function loadBin(params: { binCtx: BinOperationContext }): Promise<BinState> {
199	  // Bounded retry: convert a transient null (cold resolve cache after reload, or
200	  // a concurrent in-flight publish) into a successful load before falling back
201	  // to empty state. Never publishes.
202	  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < LOAD_BIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
203	    const loaded = await loadBinMetadataInternal({
204	      userPrivateKey: params.binCtx.userPrivateKey,
205	      ctx: params.binCtx.ctx,
206	    });
207	
208	    if (loaded) {
209	      return {
210	        entries: loaded.metadata.entries,
211	        sequenceNumber: loaded.metadata.sequenceNumber,
212	        ipnsName: loaded.ipnsName,
213	      };
214	    }
215	
216	    if (attempt < LOAD_BIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1) {
217	      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, LOAD_BIN_RETRY_DELAY_MS));
218	    }
219	  }
220	
221	  // No bin IPNS record resolved after all retries — treat as a genuinely new
222	  // bin. Return in-memory empty state WITHOUT publishing. The first addToBin
223	  // publishes at sequenceNumber 0 + 1 = 1, matching the API create-path.
224	  const binIpns = await deriveBinIpnsKeypair(params.binCtx.userPrivateKey);
225	  return {
226	    entries: [],
227	    sequenceNumber: 0,
228	    ipnsName: binIpns.ipnsName,
229	  };
230	}

232	/**
233	 * Add item to recycle bin.
234	 *
235	 * Removes the item from the folder metadata (via deleteFromFolder),
236	 * creates a BinEntry, appends to bin metadata, and publishes both.
237	 *
238	 * @returns The removed item from the folder
239	 */
240	export async function addToBin(params: {
241	  folderIpnsName: string;
242	  childId: string;
243	  parentPath: string;
244	  folderTree: FolderTree;
245	  binState: BinState;
246	  binCtx: BinOperationContext;
247	}): Promise<{ removedItem: FolderChild; updatedBinState: BinState }> {
248	  const folder = params.folderTree.get(params.folderIpnsName);
249	  if (!folder) throw new Error('Folder not loaded');
250	
251	  // 1. Remove item from folder metadata
252	  const baseChildren = [...folder.children];
253	  const { updatedChildren, removedItem } = sdkCore.deleteFromFolder({
254	    children: folder.children,
255	    childId: params.childId,
256	  });
257	
258	  // 2. Publish updated folder metadata
259	  const { newSequenceNumber, publishedChildren } = await sdkCore.updateFolderMetadataAndPublish({
260	    children: updatedChildren,
261	    baseChildren,
262	    folderKey: folder.folderKey,
263	    ipnsPrivateKey: folder.ipnsKeypair.privateKey,
264	    ipnsName: params.folderIpnsName,
265	    sequenceNumber: folder.sequenceNumber,
266	    ctx: params.binCtx.ctx,
267	  });
268	
269	  // 3. Update folder state — adopt merged published set (CR-01)
270	  folder.children = publishedChildren;
271	  folder.sequenceNumber = newSequenceNumber;
272	  folder.lastLoadedAt = Date.now();
273	  params.folderTree.set(params.folderIpnsName, folder);
274	
275	  // 4. Build bin entry
276	  const isFile = removedItem.type === 'file';
277	  const entry: BinEntry = {
278	    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
279	    itemType: isFile ? 'file' : 'folder',
280	    name: removedItem.name,
281	    originalParentIpnsName: params.folderIpnsName,
282	    originalPath: params.parentPath,
283	    deletedAt: Date.now(),
284	    size: 0,
285	    mimeType: '',
286	    filePointer: isFile ? (removedItem as FilePointer) : undefined,
287	    folderEntry: !isFile ? (removedItem as FolderEntry) : undefined,
288	  };
289	
290	  // 5. Update bin metadata and publish
291	  const updatedEntries = [...params.binState.entries, entry];
292	  const newBinSeq = params.binState.sequenceNumber + 1;
293	
294	  const metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = {
295	    version: BIN_METADATA_VERSION,
296	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
297	    entries: updatedEntries,
298	  };
299	
300	  await saveBinMetadata({ metadata, binCtx: params.binCtx });
301	
302	  const updatedBinState: BinState = {
303	    entries: updatedEntries,
304	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
305	    ipnsName: params.binState.ipnsName,
306	  };
307	
308	  return { removedItem, updatedBinState };

311	/**
312	 * Restore an item from the recycle bin back to a folder.
313	 *
314	 * Removes the entry from bin metadata, adds the preserved FolderChild
315	 * back to the target folder's children, and publishes both.
316	 */
317	export async function restoreFromBin(params: {
318	  entryId: string;
319	  targetFolderIpnsName: string;
320	  folderTree: FolderTree;
321	  binState: BinState;
322	  binCtx: BinOperationContext;
323	}): Promise<{ restoredItem: FolderChild; updatedBinState: BinState }> {
324	  // 1. Find the bin entry
325	  const entry = params.binState.entries.find((e) => e.id === params.entryId);
326	  if (!entry) throw new Error('Bin entry not found');
327	
328	  // 2. Get the FolderChild to restore
329	  let child: FolderChild;
330	  if (entry.itemType === 'file' && entry.filePointer) {
331	    child = { ...entry.filePointer, modifiedAt: Date.now() };
332	  } else if (entry.itemType === 'folder' && entry.folderEntry) {
333	    child = { ...entry.folderEntry, modifiedAt: Date.now() };
334	  } else {
335	    throw new Error('Bin entry has no stored item reference');
336	  }
337	
338	  // 3. Add child back to target folder
339	  const targetFolder = params.folderTree.get(params.targetFolderIpnsName);
340	  if (!targetFolder) throw new Error('Target folder not loaded');
341	
342	  // Handle name collisions
343	  const existingNames = new Set(targetFolder.children.map((c) => c.name));
344	  if (existingNames.has(child.name)) {
345	    let newName = `${child.name} (restored)`;
346	    let counter = 2;
347	    while (existingNames.has(newName)) {
348	      newName = `${child.name} (restored ${counter})`;
349	      counter++;
350	    }
351	    child = { ...child, name: newName };
352	  }
353	
354	  const baseChildren = [...targetFolder.children];
355	  const updatedFolderChildren = [...targetFolder.children, child];
356	
357	  // 4. Publish updated folder metadata
358	  const { newSequenceNumber, publishedChildren } = await sdkCore.updateFolderMetadataAndPublish({
359	    children: updatedFolderChildren,
360	    baseChildren,
361	    folderKey: targetFolder.folderKey,
362	    ipnsPrivateKey: targetFolder.ipnsKeypair.privateKey,
363	    ipnsName: params.targetFolderIpnsName,
364	    sequenceNumber: targetFolder.sequenceNumber,
365	    ctx: params.binCtx.ctx,
366	  });
367	
368	  // 5. Update folder state — adopt merged published set (CR-01)
369	  targetFolder.children = publishedChildren;
370	  targetFolder.sequenceNumber = newSequenceNumber;
371	  targetFolder.lastLoadedAt = Date.now();
372	  params.folderTree.set(params.targetFolderIpnsName, targetFolder);
373	
374	  // 6. Remove entry from bin and publish
375	  const remainingEntries = params.binState.entries.filter((e) => e.id !== params.entryId);
376	  const newBinSeq = params.binState.sequenceNumber + 1;
377	
378	  const metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = {
379	    version: BIN_METADATA_VERSION,
380	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
381	    entries: remainingEntries,
382	  };
383	
384	  await saveBinMetadata({ metadata, binCtx: params.binCtx });
385	
386	  const updatedBinState: BinState = {
387	    entries: remainingEntries,
388	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
389	    ipnsName: params.binState.ipnsName,
390	  };
391	
392	  return { restoredItem: child, updatedBinState };
393	}

file: packages/sdk/src/client.ts:2047  author=coderabbitai
---BODY---
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Prevent stale async completions from resurrecting unloaded shared-folder state.**

`adoptSharedFolderResult` and shared update emissions apply using a pre-await snapshot. If `unloadSharedFolder(shareId)` happens during an in-flight write/refresh, completion can reinsert state and emit `sharedFolder:updated` for a share that was explicitly unloaded.

A safe pattern is to re-read live state right before write-back/emit and no-op if absent.






<details>
<summary>Suggested fix pattern</summary>

```diff

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Zero existing key buffers before overwriting a `shareId` entry.**

`set()` replaces an existing state without clearing the previous `folderKey`/`ipnsPrivateKey`, so repeated updates can leave stale sensitive key material in memory.

<details>
<summary>🔧 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
   set(shareId: string, state: SharedFolderState): void {
+    const prev = this.shares.get(shareId);
+    if (prev) {
+      prev.folderKey.fill(0);
+      prev.ipnsPrivateKey.fill(0);
+    }
     this.shares.set(shareId, {
       ...state,
       folderKey: new Uint8Array(state.folderKey),
       ipnsPrivateKey: new Uint8Array(state.ipnsPrivateKey),
     });
   }
```
</details>

As per coding guidelines, sensitive key material should be cleared from memory after use.

  "new_string": "  /** Set or update a shared folder's state, cloning key material to avoid zeroing caller buffers */\n  set(shareId: string, state: SharedFolderState): void {\n    // Zero the previous entry's key material before overwriting so stale keys\n    // don't linger in memory across re-seeds. Guard on reference identity: the\n    // adopt path spreads the LIVE entry, so its folderKey/ipnsPrivateKey are the\n    // same buffers we're about to clone — zeroing them would corrupt the clone.\n    const prev = this.shares.get(shareId);\n    if (prev) {\n      if (prev.folderKey && prev.folderKey !== state.folderKey) prev.folderKey.fill(0);\n      if (prev.ipnsPrivateKey && prev.ipnsPrivateKey !== state.ipnsPrivateKey)\n        prev.ipnsPrivateKey.fill(0);\n    }\n    this.shares.set(shareId, {\n      ...state,\n      folderKey: new Uint8Array(state.folderKey),\n      ipnsPrivateKey: new Uint8Array(state.ipnsPrivateKey),\n    });\n  }"
}
